UObjectToolTips.FortQuestObjectiveClipboardData:
@brief Serializes quest objective data and components into JSON for clipboard storage.

This struct encapsulates quest objective data and its related extensions from quest item definition components.
When copying to the clipboard, it serializes the main objective data into a JSON object labeled "QuestObjective".
Then it iterates over each component in ObjectiveComponents, serializing each one into separate JSON object fields using
the class path of the component as the key. These serialized components are grouped together in a JSON object
labeled "QuestObjectiveExtensions". The resulting JSON string is then copied to the clipboard for storage.

When loading from the clipboard, it retrieves the JSON string and validates it. If valid, it deserializes
the main objective data from the "QuestObjective" field and each additional component from the
"QuestObjectiveExtensions" field. It constructs the Objective and ObjectiveComponents data structures
based on the deserialized data.

UObjectToolTips.FortMeshNetworkEventsLoader:
@class AFortMeshNetworkEventsLoader

The main goal of this actor is to provide an event dispatching mechanism for Fortnite and
the games built off of it. Phase 1 will be events defined in the component proper, but phase 2+
will incorporate a more general framework for event responding and communication that the game/plugins
future scripting initiatives/etc can interface with, and even a state machine defining phases
and actions within a phase (see: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1v-7PzLudd9QkAQ3Bi7B2KvQ3wbSlVYGlISTGPXXA1e0/edit?usp=sharing)

We will want to support multiple loaders that can also be tied to one/many playspace(s) that way events
can target multiple events on a single map.

There are 2 types of mesh network events that can be communicated to the Root Server that are then
disseminated out to the rest of the server/clients on the network.

MeshEventBurst - i.e. MeshNetEventBurst EventName
MeshEventStart/MeshEventEnd - i.e. MeshNetEventStart EventName and MeshNetEventEnd EventName

UObjectToolTips.FortHeldObjectComponent:
@class UFortHeldObjectComponent

      The held object component defines all the necessary functions/data to allow
      an object to become a held object. The component will implicitly grab a defined
      shape component (sphere, capsule, etc) and a defined projectile movement component. With
      these components it can handle implicitly being thrown, dropped, and placed.

      The component is setup with a generic held object weapon that defines an equip "pickup" animation,
      an ability to throw the object, and an ability to place the object. Drop happens via weapon switch, death,
      etc implicitly.

      @example: Attach this component to a BuildingGameplayActor. The BGA will override CanInteract
      and call the components CanInteract. If BGA can be held it will call OnInteract and call PickupHeldObject.

      @todo: For more fine control over pickup, placing, and throwing it would be nice to define anim
      notifies that can be assigned to an animation. Right now, attachment is done on pickup via on interact
      so it doesn't fully sync up with the weapon's equip anim. Throwing happens via a trigger event on the throw
      which looks great, but the detachment is happening via a timer, which isn't great.

UObjectToolTips.FortDownloadRequesterID:
A FFortDownloadRequesterID allows download handle retention pools, to disambiguate *unique sets* of handles under the same context.

ID's are specific to the caller, but must always represents a unique requester. The system is free to treat all requests under a given context
with a matching identifier to be treated as a separate bucket where pool settings allow.

Any single ID is not necessarily globally unique across different contexts  but should be unique within that context

The ID is implemented as a simple uint32 under the hood. FFortDownloadRequesterID offers a variety of methods to assist in
initializing this uint32  from integer, name (hashed), or gameplay tag (hashed from string), or object id depending on the requirements of the caller
UObjectToolTips.ManagerParticipantSubsetID:
A FManagerParticipantSubsetID allows a single manager implementing the QuestManager interface, to manage *multiple* unique sets of
participants to which quests can be granted, by assigning unique IDs to each subset.

ID's are context specific to any given manager, but always represents a unique group of participants that granted quests can be
scoped to within the scope of that single manager.

Any single ID is not necessarily globally unique across different managers ('1' could be widely used for example by multiple
managers to represent different participant subsets - 'squad 1' for a squad manager, or 'bounty event 1' in a bounty quest manager)

The ID is implemented as a simple uint32 under the hood. FManagerParticipantSubsetID offers a variety of methods to assist in
initializing this uint32  from integer, name (hashed), or gameplay tag (hashed from string) depending on the contextual
requirements of the implementing manager

UObjectToolTips.FortAthenaMutator_AI_SignificanceBasedUp:
A mutator used to optimize AI processing in Athena. If enabled, this mutator will batch and stagger the
tracked pawns' FortMovementComp_Character component updates so that not all components are being updated
on the same frame. The movement components are placed into buckets based on their pawn's significance. In
each bucket, movement components are divided evenly and randomly into groups (the number of groups in a
bucket equals it's FramesPerUpdate value). Only one group is updated per bucket per frame, so for a bucket
with FramesPerUpdate = 3, three groups will be created and the movement components in that bucket will be
spread evenly throughout them. Then the three groups will be updated on the next three frames (one per frame)
and the cycle will continue.

UObjectToolTips.FortDynamicRollBaseWeightTableRow:
A row in a Table that defines the base weights for items that can be rolled. This is similar to a loot table, but much simpler.
It represents a roll entry in a table of potential items to roll.
Using named weights of a loot table provides similar functionality, but has to work around specifics (ie it always adds to weights instead of replaces).
This however gives us a little more flexibility, in that we avoid duplicates and execute custom logic related to a dynamically changing loot pool.
It also provides seeded generation so that situations can be repeated and analyzed.
It also avoids needing to set up loot tiers and loot packages, which has been a blocker for creative for things in the past.
The goal of this row is to stay generic and can be used for other similar systems in the future. It was created for player augments, but has no knowledge of player augment item types.

UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderAxisProjectionOperation:
A single Axis Projection operation: gates the pose by checking that DriverBone is in front of
(or behind) TargetBone along a chosen world axis defined by AxisFrame's rotation. Useful for
pose conditions like "left thigh is in front of right thigh, relative to the pelvis":
  DriverBone = thigh_l, TargetBone = thigh_r, AxisFrame = pelvis, Axis = X, bInvert = false.

Math:
  displacement = DriverBone_world.Pos - TargetBone_world.Pos
  worldAxis    = AxisFrame_world.Rot * AxisLocal      (AxisLocal picked from Axis enum)
  projected    = dot(displacement, worldAxis)         // signed scalar in cm
  if (bInvert) projected = -projected                 // flip to test the opposite direction
  output       = clamp((projected - RemapMin) / (RemapMax - RemapMin), 0, 1)

Output is the standard 0..1 ramp the pose multiplies into its bone product. RemapMin/Max are
signed cm thresholds — bInvert flips the projection's sign before the remap, but negative
thresholds are also supported directly (e.g. RemapMin = -5, RemapMax = 0 ramps 0→1 as the
driver approaches the target from behind along the axis).
UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderDistanceOperation:
A single Distance operation: gates the pose by the world distance between DriverBone and
ReferenceBone. Math is selected by Mode (see EPoseBuilderDistanceMode).

  RelativeToRestPose (legacy):
    normalized   = current_distance / RestDistance      // 0 at ref, 1 at rest, >1 past rest
    ramp_input   = bInvert ? normalized : (1 - normalized)  // default: closer = bigger
    output       = clamp((ramp_input - RemapMin) / (RemapMax - RemapMin), 0, 1)

  AbsoluteDistance (new):
    signed_delta = current_distance - RestDistance      // +cm = further, -cm = closer
    directional  = bInvert ? -signed_delta : signed_delta
    output       = clamp((directional - RemapMin) / (RemapMax - RemapMin), 0, 1)

Raw Output published to the UI differs by mode:
  - Relative mode: the post-invert ramp input (`bInvert ? Normalized : 1-Normalized`) — the
    value that gets fed into the RemapMin/Max ramp. Useful for tuning the remap band against
    what the runtime actually sees.
  - Absolute mode: the raw signed cm delta from rest (`current_distance - RestDistance`),
    pre-invert. Shows true physical motion direction regardless of bInvert.
The two modes intentionally publish different quantities — Relative is normalized and tied
to the ramp, Absolute is a physical measurement in cm.

A single Reference operation: not a real evaluator — looks up a previously computed

UObjectToolTips.AthenaCapturePoint:
AAthenaCapturePoint
      This new building gameplay actor is the basis for all building based capture
      points.  The actor is setup to handle a plethora of capture point setups.

      Basic Rules: When a team (1+ players) steps on the capture point the point
      will flag which team is capturing and begin growing the percentage towards
      100%, when the point reaches 100% the point will lock for a defined set of
      time at which point it will unlock.

      CaptureStates: Idle is used when the point has no one on it but doesn't have
      the ability to return to 0. (Note: Useful when the decrease value is 0 to
      force the other team to drop it down to zero before gaining any control).
      Capturing is when a team is actively driving the percentage in their favor.
      Contested is when multiple teams are on the point forcing the point to contention
      based on the rules defined. Reseting is when the point has no one on it
      and has the ability to drive the percentage back to zero.

      Contention Rules: Currently there are two types of contention rules and it
      isn't hard to add more in the future. MajorityWins (default) is where the
      difference between multiple teams is the number of capturers and when an
      even number are present the point is in contention. (Note: This setup actually
      handles N teams where the team with the most and the team with the second
      most affect the difference, i.e. Team1 = 2, Team2 = 1, Team3 = 1 then Team1
      is capturing with a count of 1). OneTeamOnlyWins is where only 1 team can
      be present on the point at a time to actually capture it.

      Unlock Rules: Once the point is locked and the time interval is through and
      unlocks the point there are a couple of rules that govern how the point behaves.
      ResetState will remove the team that is controlling the point and reset all
      values to 0 so capturing can begin from the beginning again. MaintainState is
      used to keep the controlling team in ownership of the point at 100% so it is
      the other teams job to recapture the point back to 0 then back up to 100%.

UObjectToolTips.BuildingItemCollectorActor:
ABuildingItemCollectorActor

      The Building Item Collector Actor is a complex actor that can be used
      to build many different kinds of devices that players interact with
      and deposit items from their inventory.

      The Item Collector does not actually store actual inventory items. The
      actor simply verifies how many a player has, saves the total towards
      the deposit goal for that players team, then deletes those its from
      the players inventory.

      The Item Collector has various states (that may grow over time) such as FirstToGoal,
      FreeForAll.

      FirstToGoal - The objective of this behavior is for teams to deposit inventory items
      trying to be the first team to reach a desired goal value.
      When a team reaches the goal the Item Collector becomes "captured" and will no longer
      accept inventory drops until it is reset.

      Uses: BluGlo pylons in STW and Vending Machines in BR

UObjectToolTips.AthenaNavPresenceDetectorComponent:
ActorComponent that checks if one or more navigation data is/are available under the owner's location.

   It will initially broadcast NavMeshPresenceDetected or NavMeshPresenceDetected to tell if there is
   proper navigation data under owner's location (with bWasDetectedBefore/bWasUndetectedBefore = false).

   If a navigation data is not there, it will listen to newly computed nav tiles and if ever that navigation data
   become valid under the owner's location, we will broadcast the NavMeshPresenceDetected event once all the navigation data are detected (with bWasUndetectedBefore = true).

   If bDisableUponNavMeshPresence = false, if navigation data is present, it will continue listening to newly computed nav tiles and if ever the navigation data
   becomes INVALID under the owner's location, we will broadcast the NavMeshPresenceUndetected event (with bWasDetectedBefore = true).

   @note: if NavmeshNameToUse is None, it wills check against all existing AthenaNavMesh. See AthenaNavSystem.h for navmesh names to specific if needed.
   @note: if bDisableUponNavMeshPresence is True, the component Unregisters and so stops observing navigation data changes and will not refire the NavMeshPresenceDetected/NavMeshPresenceUndetected events.

cosmetic. Purely client-side and display-only: it hooks the owning skeletal mesh's
OnBoneTransformsFinalized delegate and rewrites the affected subtrees in the finalized component-space pose
each evaluation, so the scale survives animation (idle, emotes) without an anim graph or GameState
dependency. The per-bone scales are resolved per skin by the command handler.

UObjectToolTips.FortAnimNode_AimOffsets:
Aim offset node that samples the blend space during Evaluate instead of Update,
allowing the yaw & pitch coordinates to be corrected by a reference bone's local rotation
(which is only known at evaluate time, after other nodes have run).

Unlike the engine AimOffset node, this does not inherit from FAnimNode_BlendSpaceGraphBase
and therefore does not emit tick records or use sync groups. IIR filtering is applied to the
raw X,Y inputs using the blend space asset's filter settings, matching engine aim offset behavior.
UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderAimOperation:
Aim operation — a CtrlRig `AimConstraint` equivalent at the pose-driver layer. Computes how
well-aligned the driver bone's chosen local axis is with the direction toward a target, and
outputs a [0,1] alignment value the pose can use as its activation alpha.

Live evaluation each tick:
  1. AimDir   = normalize(TargetWorld.Location - AimBoneWorld.Location)
  2. ActualDir = AimBoneWorld.Rotation.RotateVector(AimAxisLocal).Normalized()
  3. Alignment = clamp((dot(ActualDir, AimDir) - InputMin) / (InputMax - InputMin), 0, 1)

`AimAxisLocal` is the local-space direction on the AimBone that should point at the target
(typical convention: +X for forward-pointing bones in UE skeletons). `InputMin/InputMax`
remap the dot product (-1..1 raw) into the meaningful range — defaults give "perpendicular
= 0, fully aimed = 1".

Mirrors `RigUnit_AimConstraint_*` minus the up-axis stabilization (which only affects rig-
applied rotation, not the alignment readout the pose driver needs).

Allows hotfixability of analytics events. You can denylist an event for a specific PlaylistName or PlaylistType (EFortGameType).
Specify the denylist type entry, then set the playlist (or type) in the PlaylistKey member,
followed by the EventName and the probability of sending it. 0 == Never send, 1 == always send.
PlaylistNames are more specific, so take precedence over a similar entry for an event in a given playlist type.

UObjectToolTips.EventObjectiveFilterCache:
An event cache is how event processors actually process registered events.
For example, when an event is registered, an event cache is created and registered with
the correct corresponding processor. Complex systems like quests register each filter
of each objective as a cache. NOTE: Objectives that have multiple filters of the same

UObjectToolTips.FortAthenaMutator_InventoryOverride_Buck:
An inventory override mutator that provides Cobalt-specific round-based loadout mechanics.
Loadouts are organized into buckets
Each round, a loadout is randomly selected for each bucket, which will be used by all players assigned to that bucket.
As long as there are at least as many buckets as players-per-team, no two players on the same team be assigned to the same bucket in a given round.
Player-bucket assignments are rotated each round so that as long as there are at least as many buckets as rounds, no player should get the same bucket twice.
Every team in given round has the same set of loadouts.

UObjectToolTips.LootInjectionOptionRow:RarityUpgrades:
Array of rarity upgrades
Each entry in this array corresponds to what LTG is unlocked AND what weights should be used to decide what rarity to actually spawn.
The weights array of the highest unlocked rarity data will be used to determine which LTG is spawned. Each value in the weights array corresponds to lowest -> highest rarity.
If the weights array is left empty, the highest level rarity upgrade unlocked will always spawn.
Example:
BaseLootTierGroup = LTG_Weapon_Common -> This is used until the player has unlocked a higher rarity
RarityUpgrades =
LootTierGroup=LTG_Weapon_Rare, Weights={0.8, 0.2} -> once unlocked, the player has an 80% chance for LTG_Weapon_Common and a 20% chance for LTG_Weapon_Rare.
LootTierGroup=LTG_Weapon_Epic, Weights={0.7, 0.2, 0.1} -> once unlocked, the player has a 70% chance for LTG_Weapon_Common, 20% chance for LTG_Weapon_Rare, 10% chance for LTG_Weapon_Epic.
OR
RarityUpgrades =
LootTierGroup=LTG_Weapon_Rare, Weights={} -> once unlocked, the player will always receive LTG_Weapon_Rare from this loot option.
LootTierGroup=LTG_Weapon_Epic, Weights={} -> once unlocked, the player will always receive LTG_Weapon_Epic from this loot option.

UObjectToolTips.QuestViewExtensionData_QuestDefinition:Q:
Associated owning quest definition for this view.
Any static data lookup should route through this component rather than occupying additional memory in the view.

This replicates the on-disk SOURCE definition, never a hotfixed RF_Transient duplicate: the
duplicate has no on-disk package, so a client cannot resolve it (Iris fails to async-load
/Engine/Transient.* and the whole quest view stalls). Producers store the source here via
FortQuestViewUtilities::GetReplicableSourceQuestDefinition; the client then upgrades it to its
own hotfixed duplicate in OnClientInitialization. If that upgrade fails the base is kept, so a
hotfixed quest degrades to its base form rather than disappearing.

UObjectToolTips.BudgetingComponent:
Base component that manages budget requests through UBudgetCategoryManager and
routes resulting status-change callbacks to per-category internal listeners.

Responsibilities:
  - Register / unregister FBudgetCandidateRequests with UBudgetCategoryManager,
    keyed by FGameplayTag CategoryId.
  - Store per-category FOnBudgetStatusChanged delegates so interested parties can
    subscribe to grant/deny outcomes without coupling directly to the manager.
  - When the manager fires a status-change callback, route it to the matching
    per-category listeners on this component.

Subclasses define which categories are meaningful and may provide typed
convenience wrappers around the registration and listener APIs.

UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderDrivenBone:bAdditive:
Blending Mode (Additive vs Override) — applies only in Default mode.
  Additive  (true, default): Accum = lerp(Identity, Transform, Output) * Accum
                             (matches AnimBP ModifyBone(Add_To_Existing) and CR
                              ModifyTransforms_PerItem(BoneOp = AdditiveLocal)).
  Override  (false):         Accum.BlendWith(Transform, Output)
                             (matches AnimBP ModifyBone(Replace_Existing) and CR
                              ModifyTransforms_PerItem(BoneOp = OverrideLocal)).

ParentConstraint mode ignores this flag — CR ParentConstraint_PerItem has no Additive/
Override distinction (it's always "lerp incoming toward constraint result by Weight").
Aim mode also ignores this flag.
Surfaced in the editor as the "Blending Mode" dropdown (Additive / Override).
UObjectToolTips.EFacialCurvesBlendPreset.BlinksAndEyeDar:
Blends the first pose expression with blinks and eye darts from the second pose. Blinks take the max value between pose while eye darts are added together.
      Output animation type will be the same as FirstPose type(3L vs Legacy) unless first pose has no facial data. Output bone transforms will always be the first pose.
UObjectToolTips.EFacialCurvesBlendPreset.AlphaCurveBlend:
Blends the first pose with the second pose based on an alpha value driven by a curve in the second pose.
      The second pose will always be evaluated to read the cure value. This allows the branch in the second pose to take control of facial animation when it needs to while
      letting the first pose come through otherwise. Non facial curves on the second pose will be ignored. Non facial curves on the first pose will pass through.
      Will not convert 3L to Legacy and vice-versa. only scale the curves according to curve alpha value
UObjectToolTips.EFacialCurvesBlendPreset.Blend:

UObjectToolTips.AudioDeviceInfo:
Blueprint accessible device data

NOTE: no C++ code references this struct - GetAudioInputDeviceInfo/GetAudioOutputDeviceInfo return
TArray<FText> from the setting view models instead. It is kept because it is a BlueprintType USTRUCT:
Blueprint variables, pins and function signatures can reference it without any C++ reference, so deleting

UObjectToolTips.BuildingActor:CullDistance:
CLIENT: Determines the rendering distance for the actor's components.
SERVER: Passed down to the replication system, which will use it to determine the distance at which
this will be replicated to a remote client.

This is dynamically calculated by UpdateCullDistance based on size of the object, using data defined
on the world settings.

It exists so that nobody has to touch every asset made or being made, so smaller things will naturally
cull at smaller ranges vs. larger objects at further ranges.

NOTE: Intentionally non-transient because this is updated during OnConstruction, which does NOT get called
in cooked builds for statically-loaded actors, meaning this will be cached at cook time.

UObjectToolTips.ECellOriginPoint:
Cell Origin Point Enum

Defines how cell coordinates map to world space positions. This affects both coordinate conversion
(world-to-cell and cell-to-world) and spatial bounds calculations for metrics collection and rendering.

- Center: Cell coordinate (0,0,0) represents the center point of the cell at world origin.

UObjectToolTips.EOratorRelevancyOverride:
Cheat-only override for the IsNetRelevantFor check applied to performance delivery.
Gates both the normal broadcast path (ForEachNetRelevantController) and the catch-up
eligibility check, so you can stage a "player out of earshot then walks in" flow
entirely through cheats: set ForceNotRelevant, start a performance with a non-None
CatchUpPolicy, then flip to ForceRelevant (or None) to have the catch-up poll deliver.
 - None: default; uses the real net relevancy result.
 - ForceNotRelevant: every controller fails the relevancy gate (suppresses both
   immediate delivery and catch-up).
 - ForceRelevant: every controller passes the relevancy gate (other gates still apply).
UObjectToolTips.EOratorCatchUpPolicyOverride:
Cheat-only override that forces a CatchUpPolicy at AddCatchUpEntry time, regardless
of the policy the caller supplied. Lets you exercise the catch-up paths in PIE without
modifying call sites that default to None.
 - NoOverride: default; honors the caller's policy.
 - ForcePolicyNone: force the performance to ignore catch-up recipients (suppresses entry insertion).
 - ForcePerformFromCurrent: force every performance to PerformFromCurrent.
 - ForcePerformFromStart: force every performance to PerformFromStart.

UObjectToolTips.SpecialEventMeshLeaderboardNetworkCompon:
Class that acts as a bridge between Leaderboard MeshNetwork dedicated servers and root server.
Properties can be replicated in the Actor [ASpecialEventMeshLeaderboardManager] from the Root all the way down to the clients.
RPCs though need to be configured in the component. Server RPCs will go up from dedicated servers to inner servers and up to the root server.

This class also reduces the number of requests made to the root server:
- Each Dedicated Server (Edge) and Intermediate Server (Inner) has an internal leaderboard of requests.
- Requests are not sent straightway. Each request is flushed after a RequestRate (seconds), collecting
 all requests from a single player in one request.
- If the request no longer meets the needed score in that time, then it's discarded.

UObjectToolTips.SpecialEventMeshLeaderboardManager:
Class that handles the Mesh Networking for a Global Leaderboard and a Local Leaderboard.
- In the Global Leaderboard it keeps track of the top [TopScorePlayersNum] scoring players in the world.
- In the Local Leaderboard it keeps track of all the players in the game session.

Features:
- It can be used both for HighScore leaderboards and LowScore leaderboards (like time attack) via ELeaderboardSortStrategy.
- Properties that are replicated in this class, will be replicated down from the Mesh Root, down to the Edge/Inner Servers and the clients.
- RPCs need to be handled via the LeaderboardMeshNetworkComponent so they can be sent up to the Root. That is used by Edge servers to send requests
 up to the root when a player scores.
- A Min Score [ScoreToEnterGlobalLeaderboard] is used to optimize the requests to the root.
- A request system is used via the LeaderboardMeshNetworkComponent, using a Request Rate, which is configurable. This way we optimize how many calls
 we sent up to the root in game modes where players can be constantly scoring. The higher the rate time, the more it takes the score to reach the root.
- Multiple properties are configurable via BP, via hotfix and via MeshCommand. This way we can do changes to the system even on Live day if needed.
- Anonymous players CAN'T reach the Leaderboard by design to follow privacy policies.

UObjectToolTips.AudioClusterAlgorithmTemplate_StaticSect:
Cluster related actors together in fixed sectors centered around the listener position. How this differs from the Dynamic Sector algorithm is
sectors here are fixed and don't depend on actor positions or the listener orientation. Actors are rather just categorized in one or the other
cluster based on which sector their position is in.

A sector is a portion of an "annulus" (a plane figure consisting of the area between a pair of concentric circles).
You will at most have N sectors, where N is the number of sectors dividing the 360deg annulus around the listener.

Sectors rotations are fixed. For example, for 4 sectors, you'll have 4 90deg sectors (because 360deg / 4 = 90deg). The first sector starting angle
can be customized.

Behavior blueprints can cast their ClusterData property to "Static Sector Audio Cluster Data" and read their cluster index that way.

Sectors positions don't rotate with the listener; they are just keeping their center aligned with it. For example, if your goal is to inform a 4.0
MetaSound based on how many actors are in each quadrant around the listener, use the UE.Spatialization MS Interface and pan your effects
accordingly.

The position of a cluster is thus that of the listener, offset radially at (OuterRadius - InnerRadius) / 2 in the direction of the half-width of
the sector. The offset from the listener is therefore fixed.
Note: This algorithm doesn't interpolate cluster positions between Fixed Updates, as it is not believed its position would be used to play a sound
directly over there. Reach out to AGE/TechAudio if you would need that!

Special cases supported:
- Single sector (ie, a 360deg annulus): Actors are part of the only cluster if their position is in the annulus.
- Disc sectors (ie, portions of a degenerate annulus where the inner circle is of radius 0): Actors are part of a sector if they are in range of
  the outer circle radius and in between the two angles defining the sector.
UObjectToolTips.AudioClusterAlgorithmTemplate_DynamicSec:
Cluster related actors together in sectors centered around the listener position. Properly supports moving actors. Allow multiple strategies for
choosing at which distance the "center" of a cluster is from the listener.
Better alternative to the legacy "Cone" algorithm.

A sector is a portion of an "annulus" (a plane figure consisting of the area between a pair of concentric circles).
The annulus starts after SectorMinRadius meters, and ends before SectorMaxRadius meters. It is then restricted to SectorWidth degrees. This gives
you a sector. Actors further than SectorMaxRadius or closer than SectorMinRadius are never clustered and are out of range for clustering.

When an actor is in range but fits no existing clusters, a new cluster is created for that actor alone, and that cluster's position is initialized
to that of the actor.

When an actor overlaps multiple clusters, it will always choose the one that's closest (excluding its current cluster IF the actor is alone in its
current cluster).

The cluster's position is such that its sector is oriented towards the geometric center of all actors it contains, at a distance from the listener
that's configurable (Center, Center weighted by actor distance, closest actor).

Clustering only happens during Fixed Updates (regularly spaced intervals, see FAudioClusterConfiguration::AlgorithmUpdateRateMs), meaning
OnActorAdded, OnStart, OnStop, OnSizeUpdated are only called at those intervals. This means that when an actor is spawned, some time might elapse
until it is properly added to a cluster. Same if an actor moves away from a cluster - its new cluster will be created at the next Fixed Update.

OnActorRemoved can be called at any time, as it happens directly when an actor is destroyed, or during the Fixed Update otherwise.

OnPositionUpdated can happen every Update (ie, every frame), as the algorithm will interpolate clusters current positions towards the target
position computed during the last Fixed Update.

UObjectToolTips.StateTreeManagerComponent:
Component responsible for creating, running, and possibly replicating StateTrees on Actors
There will only be one of these components on an Actor and will handle any/all StateTrees requested to run on the Actor

                                          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
                                         | StateTreeManagerComponent |
                                          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
               Single component attached to an Actor that will run all StateTrees for said Actor
                                                      |
                                                      |
                     -------------------------------- |---------------------------------
                     |                                |                                |
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
            | FStateTreeRuntimeData |        | FStateTreeRuntimeData |        | FStateTreeRuntimeData |
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Structures containing the runtime data required to run a UStateTreeExecutionContext (brains of the state machine)
                         and optionally replicate the state transitions to clients
                     |                                |                                |
                     |                                |                                |
                        \                             |                             /
                           \                          |                          /
                              \                       |                       /
                                 \                    |                    /
                                    \                 |                 /
                                       \              |              /
                                          \           |           /
                                             \        |        /
                                                \     |     /
                                                   \  |  /
                                                     \|/
                                           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
                                          | FStateChangeDataArray |
                                           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
     Single FastArray replicating all state changes/transitions for all StateTrees that want to replicate.
  These StateChanges will be put into their respective client-side simulation and sorted in transition order.
                                                      |
                                                     /|\
                                                   /  |  \
                                                /     |     \
                                             /        |        \
                                          /           |           \
                                       /              |              \
                                    /                 |                 \
                                 /                    |                    \
                              /                       |                       \
                           /                          |                          \
                        /                             |                             \
                     |                                |                                |
  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 | FStateTreeClientSimulationData |   | FStateTreeClientSimulationData |   | FStateTreeClientSimulationData |
  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Each FStateTreeRuntimeData that wants to replicate to clients will have a matching FStateTreeClientSimulationData.
The FStateChangeDataArray communicates the transitions from the FStateTreeRuntimeData to the respective
FStateTreeClientSimulationData. These transitions are queued up, wait for the associated UStateTreeTaskObjects to
replicate, and simulates the transition in the same order it happened in the FStateTreeRuntimeData's StateTree.

NOTE: UStateTreeTaskObjects is where the gameplay logic lives and are separately replicated subobjects who
themselves likely have replicated variables. These subobjects are referenced in the FStateChangeData and can't
be assumed to arrive at the same time that the transition made its way through this system; hence the queuing system.

NOTE: UStateTreeTaskObjects may never make their way to the client if the server began and ended the state it's
associated with before it could replicate to the client. In this situation, this replicated transition system will
skip that transition altogether and move forward to the next transition.

UObjectToolTips.MeshNetworkComponent:
Component that can be added to Actors in order to allow them to Receive properties from the Mesh Network
and to Send RPCs to the Mesh Network.

When added to an Actor, all of the Actors replicated properties will be replicated through the Mesh.
However, any RPCs on the Actor will behave as if no mesh was present (Server only goes to the Game Server,
Client only goes to the specific client, and Multicast only goes to clients connected to the Game
server).

Properties on the MeshNetworkComponet will be replicated alongside Actor Properties, just like standard replication.
But, MeshNetworkComponents only support Server and Multicast RPCs. Server RPCs go up through the Mesh
(and may be aggregated) and Multicast RPCs go down through the mesh to all clients. There is no notion
of (single) Client RPCs on the MeshNetworkComponent.
UObjectToolTips.FortAIBotSmartObjectUserComponent: Component that can be added to a AI Bot's pawn to have them use SmartObjects.
UObjectToolTips.FortAISmartObjectUserComponent:
Component that can be added to a AI pawn to have them use SmartObjects.
Replicated but only 'GetRunningSmartObject' works on clients!
The user flow is the following (plus extra optional steps):
- RunEvaluation
-- Register to internal FFortSmartObjectEvaluationResult delegates
- Call BeginSmartObjectBehavior when the AI enters the bhv scope, and so is starting to actively using the bhv [activation]
- Move to slot
- Call BeginSmartObjectInteraction when the AI is at the slot and ready to interact with the SO [running]
- Call EndSmartObjectInteraction when the AI is done interacting with the SO [end running]
- Call EndSmartObjectBehavior when the AI exits the bhv scope, and so is changing their bhv [end activation]

UObjectToolTips.FortInputBasedAFKComponent:
Component that determines whether or not a player is Away From Keyboard.

There are four "AFK States" that a player might be in:
 - Not AFK: The player is interacting with the game frequently enough that they are not considered AFK.
 - Suspected AFK: The player hasn't interacted with the game for a short time, so we start watching for signs that will prove they're not AFK.
 - Confirmed AFK: The player hasn't interacted with the game for a long time, so they are considered AFK.
 - Remained AFK: The player has been confirmed AFK for some time.

Interacting with the game in some detectable way will reset the state to "Not AFK."

This is useful in cases where we want an item definition to act like an actor when it is in a player's inventory or is stored in a pickup. The attached actor can do persistent things like show a map icon or act as an AI target.

UObjectToolTips.CosmeticDataComponent:
Component used to track individual cosmetic properties of an arbitrary type based on the actor's equipped cosmetics.

Properties are broken up into buckets based on the slot tag (for instance, a character could have a
CosmeticSlot.Backpack and CosmeticSlot.Outfit) and have property tags (such as CosmeticProperty.BackpackColor1
and CosmeticProperty.OutfitColor2).

Properties can be of any type that is derived from FCosmeticPropertyBase so plugins can easily inject new properties.

Only one property with a given type or tag can be present in a bucket at a time. If a new property with matching
type and tag is added, that property will override the existing value.

-- This is very experimental, and could change significantly as we add more concrete use cases. Use only if you're
okay with that! --

This Game Framework Component can be added onto any Actor to provide support for the actor being in various phases
Phases are defined by Targeted reactions that are granted when the phase is entered, and Conditionals that when met will

to client, where the client will process the transition for the new phase as well.

any Verse-added input bindings and mapping contexts when a minigame ends.

This prevents stale UInputAction references from blocking Game Feature Plugin
unmounting during release swaps on the dedicated server.
UObjectToolTips.PlayerControllerComponent_QuestManager:
Controller component that owns and exposes the IQuestManager instance for one player.
Responsible for GC ownership (via UPROPERTY) and discovery (via FindComponentByClass).
Other systems acquire the manager by querying this component from the controller.

QuestManagerClass must be set to a class that implements IQuestManager.
The manager is instantiated in BeginPlay and its collection is registered with the
quest subsystem. The IQuestParticipant is owned by the sibling
UPlayerControllerComponent_QuestParticipant.
UObjectToolTips.PlayerControllerComponent_QuestParticipa:
Controller component that owns and exposes the IQuestParticipant instance for one player.
Responsible for GC ownership (via UPROPERTY) and discovery (via FindComponentByClass).
Other systems acquire the participant by querying this component from the controller.

QuestParticipantClass must be set to a class that implements IQuestParticipant.
The participant is instantiated in BeginPlay and bound to the owning controller.
UObjectToolTips.FortControllerComponent_NPCMapMarkers:
Controller component that receives live NPC world positions from the server while the
Character Collection Screen is open. Uses a replicated FastArraySerializer driven by
UFortNPCMapMarkerWorldSubsystem. Subscription is ref counted by named reason via
ServerAddSubscription / ServerRemoveSubscription so multiple client-side consumers can
share the stream; the server pushes updates only while at least one reason is active

UObjectToolTips.FortControllerComponent_ArcadeMinigame:
Controller-attached component that manages a single player's arcade-game session.

  Server side:
    - Observes pawn death (via UFortControllerComponent::OnPawnDied) so dying
      mid-arcade ends the session cleanly.

  Client side (via RPC):
    - Pushes a UDynamicUIScene to the UDynamicUIManager for the local player.
    - Pushes a UInputMappingContext + binds the exit input action.

The scene declares the widget(s) to display via its Allowed list; this component
never instantiates widgets directly.

Cabinet BGAs hold a UDynamicUIScene reference. On BlueprintOnInteract they call
GetForPlayer(InteractingPC)->BeginSession(Scene).

UObjectToolTips.FortDebugFreeCamera:
Debug free camera controlled via gamepad or keyboard/mouse.

Gamepad controls:
  Left Stick        — Move (forward/back, strafe)
  Right Stick       — Look (yaw/pitch)
  Left Bumper       — Decrease speed
  Right Bumper      — Increase speed
  Left Trigger      — Move down (Z)
  Right Trigger     — Move up (Z)
  D-Pad Up          — Toggle between Flying and Frozen (freeze camera, return player control)
  Start + L3        — Toggle debug camera on/off
  R3                — Toggle on-screen control display

Keyboard/mouse controls:
  W / S             — Move forward / back
  A / D             — Strafe left / right
  Q / E             — Move down / up (Z)
  Mouse             — Look (yaw/pitch)
  Mouse Wheel       — Decrease / Increase speed

Gamepad and keyboard inputs are additive and clamped to [-1, 1].

Opt-in: console command "ToggleFreeCamera" (bindable via setbind). Once used, Start+L3 shortcut stays active for the session.
All functionality is compiled out of shipping builds (WITH_CHEAT_MANAGER).

UObjectToolTips.PlayspaceComponent_DormancyManager:
Dormancy Manager component for Playspaces

This component will automatically handle the dormancy of its containing Playspace based on the amount of users within that Playspace.

When there are no users in the Playspace, that Playspace will be network dormant. When any users enter the Playspace, that Playspace will leave
network dormancy. (Although, the specific dormancy states are user-controlled via properties)

Use cases include:
Default: Initial = DORM_Initial, Awoken = DORM_Awake, Asleep = DORM_DormantAll  - (as described above)

Selectively Awoken: Initial = DORM_Initial, Awoken = DORM_DormantPartial, Asleep = DORM_DormantAll
    - When awoken, still dormant for some connections

Selectively Asleep:  Initial = DORM_DormantPartial, Awoken = DORM_Awake, Asleep = DORM_DormantPartial
 - While asleep, still non-dormant for some connections

multi-navmesh generator. Drop one into a level and tune TransitionSpacingUU to
densify (smaller) or sparsen (larger) cross-mesh links wherever the volume
overlaps a candidate transition's projected location on either sub-navmesh.

Resolution rule (in the generator's SampleColumn): if either side's projection
lies inside this volume's brush, the volume's TransitionSpacingUU replaces the

wins. Build-time only — runtime moves of the volume don't auto-rebuild.

Energy channels that have just been added this frame.  They are guaranteed to last at least one frame, and won't
be removed until they've acted.  NOTE: Currently only EnergyChannels that are USING energy, not ADDING energy,
are put in this array.  That's because we want to guarantee we don't add and then remove in the same frame and
so dodge the energy use, but at the moment we're not concerned with exploits dodging the addition of energy.
If some use-case arises where it is an exploit to dodge adding energy, we can add those through this intermediary
as well.

UObjectToolTips.RigUnit_PoseBuilder:
Evaluates a UPoseBuilderAsset against the current rig state.

Per-tick pipeline (see Execute() in RigUnit_PoseBuilder.cpp):
  1. Cache validation. Flat-index FCachedRigElement arrays for drivers, driven bones,
     DeltaRef bases, parent bones, and curves are rebuilt when bone counts, pose order
     (ReorderVersion), or any referenced bone key changes (LastBoneKeyHash).
  2. Per-pose driver evaluation. Each driver runs SPR ellipse math (DriverMode::SPR) or
     DeltaRef component extraction (DriverMode::DeltaRef) and the AND-product of all the
     pose's driver weights becomes that pose's activation. Optional FInterpTo smoothing
     can be applied via bAlphaInterpEnabled. PoseWeight (or its bound CR variable) acts
     as a final-output multiplier; a bool variable bound to FALSE short-circuits the
     entire pose for performance. Edit-Driven-Bone Isolate also short-circuits all
     non-edited poses.
  3. Unified blend pass. Driven bones (Default mode = stored offset, ParentConstraint
     mode = weighted parent blend) are blended on top of a baseline of rest transforms.
     Poses are processed in ascending Priority order so higher-Priority poses overwrite
     lower-Priority contributions on shared bones.
  4. Curve writeback. Each pose's DrivenCurves are set to that pose's activation weight,
     with disabled / edit-mode poses skipped (no curve write at all, so other systems
     driving the same curve aren't fought).
  5. Debug draw. SPR manifolds for the eye-button driver, blend-active drivers, and the
     active Driver Bone Edit Mode driver. Manifolds are filtered by DriverActivationWeights so only
     drivers actually inside their active region are drawn.

Editor-only state on UPoseBuilderAsset (EditModePoseSlot plus EditorState.ActiveEdit
for the four mutually-exclusive sub-edit-modes) gates evaluation paths so the
rig unit and details panel cooperate without fighting over preview transforms.

UObjectToolTips.FortWorldConditionStateComponent:
Evaluates world condition queries driven by data registries and applies gameplay tags + fires BP events
when condition results change.

Supports two types of checks (both can be active simultaneously):
- Actor-only: evaluated once per tick with just the owner actor as context.
- Per-nearby-actor: evaluated per nearby actor each tick. Uses UFortNearbyActorsPerceptionComponent
  on the owner to detect nearby actors. The perception config defaults to real players but can be
  changed in the editor.

Each row in the data registries has an optional SelectionPrecondition that is re-evaluated each
tick until it passes, then permanently activated. This lazy activation handles cases where the
ASC or tags are not ready at spawn. It also allows a single shared data table to serve many
different actors, with per-row filtering.

NOTE: For per-nearby-actor evaluation, this component requires a UFortNearbyActorsPerceptionComponent
on the owning actor. If the actor is an AI/NPC pawn, use UFortAINearbyActorsPerceptionComponent instead
(which provides AI LOD integration). The component will ensure on BeginPlay if it is missing.

Event reaction that modifies a tag container global variable by adding, removing, setting, or clearing tags.

Tag Container Operations:
This reaction provides full CRUD operations on tag container variables:
- **Add**: Insert tags into existing container (union operation)
- **Remove**: Delete specific tags from container (difference operation)
- **Set**: Replace entire container contents (assignment operation)
- **Clear**: Empty the container (reset operation)

Common Use Cases:
- **Buff System**: Add/remove buff tags ("Buff.Strength", "Buff.Speed")
- **Status Effects**: Track active effects ("Status.Burning", "Status.Frozen")
- **Permission System**: Grant/revoke permissions ("Permission.Build", "Permission.Admin")
- **Unlock System**: Add unlocked content tags ("Unlocked.Weapon.Rifle", "Unlocked.Ability.Dash")
- **Quest System**: Track completed objectives ("Quest.Objective.1", "Quest.Objective.2")
- **State Tracking**: Monitor active states ("State.InCombat", "State.Sprinting")

Example Scenarios:
- **Grant buff**: Operation=Add, Tags={"Buff.Damage.10Percent"}
- **Remove debuff**: Operation=Remove, Tags={"Debuff.Slowed"}
- **Set permissions**: Operation=Set, Tags={"Permission.Build", "Permission.Edit"}
- **Clear all buffs**: Operation=Clear (TagsToModify ignored)
- **Add multiple statuses**: Operation=Add, Tags={"Status.Poison", "Status.Weakened"}
- **Unlock abilities**: Operation=Add, Tags={"Ability.Dash", "Ability.DoubleJump"}

Storage Scope:
Variables can be scoped to different storage levels:
- World scope: Shared globally (e.g., world events, global unlocks)
- Actor scope: Per-actor (e.g., character buffs, player permissions)
- LevelInstance scope: Shared within level instance

Operation Details:

**Add Operation:**
- Adds tags to the existing set
- Duplicate tags are automatically ignored (sets don't allow duplicates)
- If container doesn't exist, creates it with these tags
- Example: Container has {A, B}, Add {B, C} → Result: {A, B, C}

**Remove Operation:**
- Removes specified tags if present
- Tags not in the container are silently ignored
- If container doesn't exist, no operation
- Example: Container has {A, B, C}, Remove {B, D} → Result: {A, C}

**Set Operation:**
- Completely replaces container contents
- All previous tags are discarded
- If container doesn't exist, creates it with these tags
- Example: Container has {A, B, C}, Set {D, E} → Result: {D, E}

**Clear Operation:**
- Removes all tags, creating an empty container
- TagsToModify is not used for this operation
- If container doesn't exist, creates empty container
- Example: Container has {A, B, C}, Clear → Result: {}

Integration:
Modified tag containers can be queried using:
- FGameplayProviderTagContainer_GlobalVariable to retrieve the container
- Tag queries to check for specific tags or patterns
- HasTag/HasAny/HasAll operations for conditional logic

@see FGlobalVariableType_TagContainer for the variable type this reaction modifies
@see FGameplayProviderTagContainer_GlobalVariable for reading tag containers
@see GlobalVariableUtils::GetGlobalVariableTagContainer for querying containers
UObjectToolTips.FortEventReaction_UpdateInt32Variable:
FFortEventReaction_UpdateInt32Variable

Event reaction that updates an int32 global variable based on the triggering conditional's delta value.

Behavior:
- Extracts delta from the triggering conditional (FGameplayConditionalReactionData)
- Converts delta to int32 (truncates fractional part)
- Optionally multiplies by a numerical provider value
- Adds the final value to the int32 global variable

Delta Source:
The delta comes from the conditional that triggered this reaction. Conditionals track the
change in their measured value (e.g., health decreased by 25, score increased by 100).
This reaction applies that delta to a different variable.

Use Cases:
- Damage tracking: When health decreases, add damage amount to TotalDamageTaken
- Score accumulation: When points awarded, add to lifetime score
- Kill tracking: When enemy count decreases, increment EnemiesDefeated
- Resource consumption: When ammo used, track total AmmoExpended
- Progress milestones: When objectives completed, increment TotalCompletedObjectives

Example Scenarios:
- Health damage: Conditional monitors Health, on decrease, add delta to DamageTaken variable
- Points earned: Conditional tracks Score, on increase, add delta to LifetimePoints
- Combo counter: Conditional checks combo, on increase, add delta to ComboTotal
- Resource spent: Conditional monitors Gold, on decrease, add delta to GoldSpent
- Enemy progression: Conditional tracks EnemiesRemaining, on decrease, add to EnemiesKilled

Multiplier:
The optional multiplier allows scaling the delta before applying it:
- Difficulty multiplier: Multiply damage by difficulty factor
- Bonus multiplier: Apply 2x multiplier during bonus period
- Team split: Divide points by team size (using fraction < 1)
- Scaling: Apply percentage modifiers

Multiplier Examples:
- bUseMultiplier=true, Multiplier=2.0 → Delta of 10 becomes 20
- bUseMultiplier=true, Multiplier=0.5 → Delta of 10 becomes 5
- bUseMultiplier=true, Multiplier from DifficultyLevel variable → Dynamic scaling

Conversion:
Both delta and multiplier are converted to int32:
- Delta of 25.7 → 25 (truncated)
- Delta of 10.0 * Multiplier of 1.5 = 15.0 → 15
- Fractional parts are discarded (not rounded)

@see FGlobalVariableModifier_AddInt32Value for the underlying modifier used
@see FGlobalVariableType_Int32 for the variable type this reaction modifies
@see FGameplayConditionalReactionData for conditional delta source
UObjectToolTips.FortEventReaction_UpdateNumericVariable:
FFortEventReaction_UpdateNumericVariable

Event reaction that updates a numeric (double) global variable based on the triggering conditional's delta value.

Behavior:
- Extracts delta from the triggering conditional (FGameplayConditionalReactionData)
- Delta is a double value (preserves fractional precision)
- Optionally multiplies by a numerical provider value
- Adds the final value to the numeric global variable

Numeric vs Int32:
This reaction operates on FGlobalVariableType_Numeric (double-precision floating-point) variables.
Use this instead of UpdateInt32Variable when you need:
- Fractional values and precision (percentages, multipliers, rates)
- Large value ranges beyond int32 limits
- Smooth accumulation of small changes
- Mathematical operations requiring decimal accuracy

Delta Source:
The delta comes from the conditional that triggered this reaction. Conditionals track the
change in their measured value (e.g., health percentage decreased by 0.25, speed multiplier
increased by 0.1). This reaction applies that delta to a different variable.

Use Cases:
- Percentage tracking: Track cumulative percentage changes
- Multiplier accumulation: Add buff multipliers progressively
- Rate calculations: Accumulate rates and speeds
- Precise metrics: Track exact damage amounts with decimals
- Smooth progression: Gradual stat increases (0.01 per frame)
- Financial systems: Currency with decimal places

Example Scenarios:
- Buff stacking: Conditional tracks buff strength, add delta to TotalBuffMultiplier
- Stamina drain: Conditional monitors stamina rate, add drain amount to TotalStaminaUsed
- Precision damage: Track exact damage including decimal amounts (25.75 damage)
- Speed accumulation: Track total speed bonuses applied (0.15 + 0.25 + 0.1)
- Quest progress: Accumulate partial progress percentages (0.33 + 0.67 = 1.0)

Multiplier:
The optional multiplier allows scaling the delta before applying it:
- Efficiency modifier: Multiply resource usage by efficiency (0.8 = 20% more efficient)
- Bonus multiplier: Apply 1.5x multiplier during events
- Scaling factors: Apply percentage modifiers (0.25 for 25% reduction)
- Dynamic adjustments: Scale based on current game state

Multiplier Examples:
- bUseMultiplier=true, Multiplier=2.0 → Delta of 0.5 becomes 1.0
- bUseMultiplier=true, Multiplier=0.75 → Delta of 1.0 becomes 0.75
- bUseMultiplier=true, Multiplier from EventBonus variable → Dynamic scaling

Precision:
Both delta and multiplier retain full double precision:
- Delta of 0.125 * Multiplier of 1.5 = 0.1875 (exact)
- No truncation or rounding loss
- Suitable for accumulating many small changes

@see FGlobalVariableModifier_AddNumericalValue for the underlying modifier used
@see FGlobalVariableType_Numeric for the variable type this reaction modifies
@see FGameplayConditionalReactionData for conditional delta source
@see FFortEventReaction_UpdateInt32Variable for integer variable updates

UObjectToolTips.FortMoveCollisionProbeSetup:
FFortMoveCollisionProbeSetup are used to check outside of the main collision Capsule of the character, to determine if there are
undesirable penetrations on parts of the body that extend outside of that capsule. The actual Probe should be added
as a PrimitiveComponent with a named tag, matching the ProbeTag entry on this setup.
 * The probe will be swept every other frame (or with an optional DelayBetweenProbes delay)
 * The probe is swept from the Actor root to the component location on the Actor, vs ProbeSweepTypes object types.
 * Any blocking collision found is applied to our movement as an additional InputVector away from the collision.
 * The strength of that input is the penetration depth along the sweep, times AvoidanceStrength (scales up the more it penetrates).

UObjectToolTips.FortRichFoleyContextCacheEntry:

UObjectToolTips.GameplayProviderNumerical_GlobalVariable:
FGameplayProviderNumerical_GlobalVariable_Int32

Numerical provider that retrieves an int32 value from a global variable and casts it to double.

Behavior:
- If the variable exists: Returns the int32 value cast to double (preserves value exactly)
- If the variable doesn't exist: Returns backup provider value (if configured), or empty optional

Type Conversion:
This provider reads FGlobalVariableType_Int32 variables and converts them to double for use
in numerical calculations. The conversion is lossless for int32 values since double can
represent all 32-bit integers exactly.

Storage Scope:
Variables can be scoped to different storage levels:
- World scope: Shared across the entire world/level
- Actor scope: Specific to an individual actor
- LevelInstance scope: Shared within a level instance
The scope determines where the variable is stored and retrieved from.

Use Cases:
- Read counters: KillCount, CollectedItems, CompletedObjectives
- Query scores: CurrentScore, HighScore, TotalPoints
- Check progress: CurrentLevel, WaveNumber, RemainingLives
- Conditionals: Use in math operations or comparisons (e.g., if Score > 1000)
- Dynamic calculations: Multiply DamageBase * DifficultyLevel

Example Scenarios:
- Award bonus: Calculate BonusPoints = BaseReward * (KillCount / 10)
- Scale difficulty: SpawnRate = BaseRate + (WaveNumber * 2)
- Progress gates: Unlock door when CollectedKeys >= RequiredKeys
- Dynamic pricing: Cost = BasePrice + (PurchaseCount * 10)

Backup Value:
If the variable doesn't exist and bUseBackupValueIfVariableDoesntExist is true,
the BackupValue provider is evaluated instead. This allows default values or
fallback calculations when variables haven't been initialized yet.

@see FGlobalVariableType_Int32 for the variable type this provider reads
@see FGameplayProviderNumerical for the base numerical provider interface
@see GlobalVariableUtils::GetGlobalVariableInt32 for the underlying lookup function
UObjectToolTips.GameplayProviderTagContainer_GlobalVaria:
FGameplayProviderTagContainer_GlobalVariable

Tag container provider that retrieves a gameplay tag container from a global variable.

Behavior:
- If the variable exists: Returns the tag container stored in the global variable
- If the variable doesn't exist: Returns backup provider value (if configured), or empty optional

Tag Container Variables:
This provider reads FGlobalVariableType_TagContainer variables, which store collections
of gameplay tags. Tag containers are useful for:
- Dynamic state tracking (multiple active buffs, debuffs, or conditions)
- Capability sets (unlocked abilities, available items, granted permissions)
- Filtering and matching (checking for specific tags or tag queries)
- Event categorization (tracking multiple simultaneous event types)

Storage Scope:
Variables can be scoped to different storage levels:
- World scope: Shared across the entire world/level
- Actor scope: Specific to an individual actor
- LevelInstance scope: Shared within a level instance
The scope determines where the variable is stored and retrieved from.

Use Cases:
- Read active buffs: Retrieve all buffs currently applied to a character
- Check capabilities: Get set of unlocked abilities or permissions
- Query conditions: Check if specific tags are present (e.g., HasTag("Status.Stunned"))
- Filter by criteria: Match tag queries against the container
- Display states: Show all active status effects in UI
- Conditional logic: Branch based on tag presence or absence

Example Scenarios:
- Buff system: Read "ActiveBuffs" container to display all current buffs
- Permission check: Query "PlayerPermissions" to see if "Permission.Build" is granted
- Status effects: Read "StatusEffects" to check for "Effect.Poison" or "Effect.Shield"
- Unlock system: Get "UnlockedAbilities" container for ability UI
- Quest tracking: Read "CompletedObjectives" tags to determine quest progress

Tag Container Operations:
The returned container can be used with:
- HasTag() / HasAny() / HasAll() - Check for specific tags
- Matches() - Test against tag queries
- Filter() - Get subset matching criteria
- Count() - Get number of tags
- Iteration - Loop through all tags

Backup Value:
If the variable doesn't exist and bUseBackupValueIfVariableDoesntExist is true,
the BackupValue provider is evaluated instead. Common backup patterns:
- Empty container - Default to no tags
- Fixed tag set - Default initial tags
- Another GlobalVariable - Fallback to different container

@see FGlobalVariableType_TagContainer for the variable type this provider reads
@see FGameplayProviderTagContainer for the base tag container provider interface
@see GlobalVariableUtils::GetGlobalVariableTagContainer for the underlying lookup function
UObjectToolTips.GameplayQuery_BoolGlobalVariable:
FGameplayQuery_BoolGlobalVariable

Query that checks if a boolean global variable matches an expected value.

Query Result:
- Returns **Passed** if the variable value == bExpectedValue
- Returns **Failed** if the variable value != bExpectedValue
- If variable doesn't exist: Uses bTreatMissingVariableAs for the comparison

Behavior Examples:
- Variable = true, Expected = true → **Passed**
- Variable = false, Expected = true → **Failed**
- Variable = true, Expected = false → **Failed**
- Variable = false, Expected = false → **Passed**
- Variable doesn't exist, TreatMissingAs = false, Expected = false → **Passed**
- Variable doesn't exist, TreatMissingAs = false, Expected = true → **Failed**

Storage Scope:
Variables can be scoped to different storage levels:
- World scope: Shared across the entire world/level
- Actor scope: Specific to an individual actor (requires participant object)
- LevelInstance scope: Shared within a level instance

Use Cases:
- Feature gate checks: Query if "FeatureEnabled" is true before allowing action
- State validation: Check if "IsDoorOpen" is true to allow passage
- Requirement checks: Verify "HasCompletedTutorial" is true for advanced features
- Negative checks: Query if "IsLocked" is false (using bExpectedValue = false)
- Conditional logic: Branch behavior based on global bool flags
- System toggles: Check if debug mode or admin mode is enabled

Example Scenarios:
- Quest gating: Check if "Quest.IsActive" is true before showing objectives
- Door interaction: Query "Door.IsUnlocked" is true to allow opening
- Tutorial skip: Check if "Player.HasSeenTutorial" is true to skip intro
- Feature flag: Query "Features.NewCombatSystem" is true to enable new mechanics
- Admin actions: Check if "Player.IsAdmin" is true for admin commands
- Negative condition: Query "World.GameOver" is false to continue gameplay

Missing Variable Handling:
The bTreatMissingVariableAs property provides graceful handling for uninitialized variables:
- Set to false (default): Missing variables are treated as false (safe default)
- Set to true: Missing variables are treated as true (opt-in behavior)
- This allows queries to work before variables are explicitly initialized

Common Patterns:
- Check for true: Expected=true, TreatMissing=false (requires explicit true)
- Check for false: Expected=false, TreatMissing=false (default is considered false)
- Opt-out flag: Expected=false, TreatMissing=true (must explicitly set to false)
- Opt-in flag: Expected=true, TreatMissing=false (must explicitly set to true)

Integration:
This query can be used in:
- FGlobalVariableModifier_LogicalOperation (as operand query)
- Conditional reactions and modifiers
- Gameplay ability requirements
- State machine conditions
- UI visibility rules

@see FGlobalVariableType_Bool for the variable type this query reads
@see FGameplayQuery for the base query interface
@see GlobalVariableUtils::GetGlobalVariableBool for the underlying lookup function
UObjectToolTips.GameplayQuery_DistanceInRange:
FGameplayQuery_DistanceInRange

Checks if the distance between the contextual object and query object is within a specified range.

Both objects are resolved to their best location actor using the standard resolution chain:
APawn > AActor > UActorComponent owner (recursive). This ensures that controllers, player states,
and components are correctly resolved to actors with valid world positions.

Query Result:
- Returns **Passed** when the distance between the two resolved actors falls within DistanceRange
- Returns **Failed** when the distance is outside DistanceRange
- Returns **Failed** when either object cannot be resolved to a valid actor

Distance Modes:
- 3D Distance (default): Full Euclidean distance including vertical separation
- 2D Distance: Horizontal-only distance ignoring Z axis, useful for ground-based checks

Use Cases:
- Proximity triggers: Check if player is within 500 units of an objective
- Attack range validation: Verify target is within weapon effective range
- Interaction distance: Confirm player is close enough to interact with an object
- Safe zone checks: Determine if actor is within a distance band (e.g., between 200 and 1000 units)
- AI awareness: Check if AI should notice a nearby player

Example Scenarios:
- DistanceRange = [0, 500], bUse2DDistance = false -> Passed if within 500 units in 3D
- DistanceRange = (1000, +inf), bUse2DDistance = true -> Passed if more than 1000 units away horizontally
- DistanceRange = [200, 800] -> Passed if between 200 and 800 units (inclusive)

@see GameplayQueryUtilities::ResolveLocationActor for the actor resolution chain
@see FGameplayQuery_IsNumericalValueInRange for generic numerical range checks
@see FGameplayQuery_IsFacing for directional spatial checks
UObjectToolTips.GameplayQuery_IsFacing:
FGameplayQuery_IsFacing

Checks if the contextual object is facing the query object within a specified angle cone.

The facing check computes the angle between the contextual actor's forward vector and
the direction toward the query actor. If this angle is within AngleTolerance degrees,
the query passes.

Both objects are resolved to their best location actor using the standard resolution chain:
APawn > AActor > UActorComponent owner (recursive).

Query Result:
- Returns **Passed** when the angle from the contextual actor's forward vector to
  the direction of the query actor is less than or equal to AngleTolerance
- Returns **Failed** when the angle exceeds AngleTolerance
- Returns **Failed** when either object cannot be resolved to a valid actor
- Returns **Failed** when both actors are at the same location (direction is zero)

Angle Modes:
- 2D Angle (default): Ignores vertical (Z) component, checks horizontal facing only
- 3D Angle: Full 3D angle including pitch, useful for flying or vertical aiming checks

Use Cases:
- Detection systems: Check if an AI is looking toward the player
- Stealth mechanics: Verify a player is not in an enemy's line of sight cone
- Interaction validation: Ensure a player is facing an interactable object
- Aim assist: Determine if a player is roughly aimed at a target
- Backstab mechanics: Invert the query to check if an attacker is behind the target

Example Scenarios:
- AngleTolerance = 45, bUse2DAngle = true -> Passes if facing within 45 degrees horizontally
- AngleTolerance = 90, bUse2DAngle = true -> Passes if target is in front hemisphere
- AngleTolerance = 10, bUse2DAngle = false -> Tight 3D cone, useful for precise aiming
- AngleTolerance = 180 -> Always passes (full sphere)

@see GameplayQueryUtilities::ResolveLocationActor for the actor resolution chain
@see FGameplayQuery_DistanceInRange for distance-based spatial checks
@see FGameplayQuery_LineOfSight for visibility-based checks
UObjectToolTips.GameplayQuery_IsObjectiveActive:
FGameplayQuery_IsObjectiveActive

Checks if a specific quest objective is currently active for the query object.

Looks up the specified quest on the query object and checks whether the named objective
is currently active (in progress). The query object is passed directly to the quest
utilities — it does not need to be an actor. Any quest-owning object is supported
(players, game state, NPCs, or any object implementing the quest participant interface).

The quest definition is selected in the editor, and the objective is chosen from a dropdown
populated from that quest's objectives via a property type customization.

Query Result:
- Returns **Passed** when the specified objective on the quest is active for the query object
- Returns **Failed** when the objective is not active (not started, completed, or quest not found)
- Returns **Failed** when the query object is null
- Returns **Failed** when the quest definition is not set or not loaded
- Returns **Failed** when the objective backend name is not set

Use Cases:
- Quest gating: Only allow actions when a specific objective is in progress
- Objective-driven events: Trigger reactions when an objective becomes the active step
- Conditional UI: Show or hide UI elements based on current quest progress
- NPC behavior: Change NPC dialogue or actions based on player's active objective

@see FGameplayConditional_QuestState for event-driven quest state monitoring
@see QuestUtilities::FindQuestFromDefinition for the quest lookup mechanism
UObjectToolTips.GameplayQuery_NearbyActorsOfType:
FGameplayQuery_NearbyActorsOfType

Checks if actors matching a class and/or tag filter exist within a search radius of the
contextual object.

Performs a sphere overlap test centered on the contextual actor's location with the
specified SearchRadius. Overlapping actors are filtered by ActorClass and/or TagQuery.
The query passes if the count of matching actors falls within RequiredCount.

The contextual object is resolved to its best location actor using the standard resolution chain:
APawn > AActor > UActorComponent owner (recursive).

Query Result:
- Returns **Passed** when the number of matching nearby actors falls within RequiredCount
- Returns **Failed** when the count is outside RequiredCount (too few or too many)
- Returns **Failed** when the contextual object cannot be resolved to a valid actor
- Returns **Failed** when the world context cannot be obtained

Filter Modes:
- ActorClass only: Matches actors of the specified class (and derived classes by default)
- ActorClass + bExactClassMatch: Matches only the exact class, excluding derived classes
- TagQuery only: Matches actors whose tags pass the query
- Both (bRequireBothFilters): Actor must match BOTH class and tag filters
- Both (!bRequireBothFilters): Actor must match EITHER class or tag filter

Use Cases:
- Area awareness: Check if enemies are within detection range
- Proximity triggers: Verify at least 2 teammates are nearby
- Environmental checks: Detect if destructible objects are within blast radius
- Crowd detection: Check if too many players are in a small area

@see FGameplayQuery_DistanceInRange for checking distance to a specific actor
@see GameplayQueryUtilities::ResolveLocationActor for the actor resolution chain

UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_AddInt32Value:
FGlobalVariableModifier_AddInt32Value

Modifier that adds a value to an int32 global variable (relative modification).

Behavior:
- If the variable exists: NewValue = CurrentValue + ValueToAdd (delta equals ValueToAdd)
- If the variable doesn't exist: Creates variable with value 0, then adds (NewValue = 0 + ValueToAdd)

Value Providers:
Uses FGameplayProviderNumerical to support both fixed and dynamic values:
- Fixed values: Hardcoded increment/decrement amounts
- Dynamic values: Calculate add amount from other variables, conditionals, etc.
- Negative values: Use negative numbers to subtract (e.g., -10 decreases by 10)

Delta Tracking:
The delta after this modifier is always equal to the value added:
- Add +5 to variable: Delta = +5 (regardless of starting value)
- Add -3 to variable: Delta = -3 (subtraction shows as negative delta)
- This makes AddInt32Value ideal for tracking incremental changes

Use Cases:
- Increment counters: Add +1 to KillCount on enemy defeat
- Decrement resources: Add -10 to AmmoCount on weapon fire
- Award points: Add +100 to Score on objective completion
- Apply damage: Add -25 to HealthPoints (or use negative for damage)
- Progress tracking: Add +1 to QuestProgress on milestone
- Dynamic adjustments: Add calculated value based on difficulty multiplier

Example Scenarios:
- Kill tracking: Add +1 to EnemiesDefeated on each kill
- Combo system: Add +(ComboLevel * 10) to Score
- Resource consumption: Add -1 to RemainingLives on death
- Difficulty scaling: Add +(WaveNumber * 5) to SpawnCount
- Conditional rewards: Add +(Bonus ? 50 : 10) to Points using provider

Integer Overflow:
- Standard C++ integer overflow behavior applies (wrapping)
- INT_MAX + 1 wraps to INT_MIN
- INT_MIN - 1 wraps to INT_MAX
- For overflow protection, validate values in your gameplay logic or use clamping providers

@see FGlobalVariableModifier_SetInt32Value for setting absolute values
@see FGlobalVariableModifier_Int32MathOperation for multiplication, division, min, max operations
@see FGameplayProviderNumerical for available value provider types
@see FGlobalVariableType_Int32 for the variable type this modifier operates on
UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_AddNumericalValue:
FGlobalVariableModifier_AddNumericalValue

Modifier that adds a floating-point value to a Numeric global variable (relative modification with precision).

Behavior:
- If the variable exists: NewValue = CurrentValue + ValueToAdd (delta equals ValueToAdd)
- If the variable doesn't exist: Creates variable with value 0.0, then adds (NewValue = 0.0 + ValueToAdd)

Numeric vs Int32:
This modifier operates on FGlobalVariableType_Numeric (double-precision floating-point) variables,
as opposed to FGlobalVariableModifier_AddInt32Value which operates on integer variables.

Use Numeric variables when you need:
- Fractional values (0.5, 3.14, 0.001, etc.)
- High precision for accumulating small changes
- Smooth interpolation values (percentages, multipliers, normalized values)
- Large value ranges beyond int32 limits

Value Providers:
Uses FGameplayProviderNumerical to support both fixed and dynamic values:
- Fixed values: Hardcoded increment/decrement amounts (can be fractional)
- Dynamic values: Calculate add amount from other variables, conditionals, etc.
- Negative values: Use negative numbers to subtract (e.g., -0.5 decreases by 0.5)

Delta Tracking:
The delta after this modifier equals the value added:
- Add +1.5 to variable: Delta = +1.5
- Add -0.25 to variable: Delta = -0.25
- Fractional deltas are preserved with full precision

Use Cases:
- Accumulate percentages: Add +0.05 to CritChance (5% increase)
- Smooth multipliers: Add +0.1 to SpeedMultiplier
- Resource depletion: Add -0.01 to Stamina per frame
- Precise calculations: Health percentages, damage modifiers, interpolation values
- Score accumulation: Add fractional points for partial objectives
- Physics values: Velocity, acceleration, force magnitudes

Example Scenarios:
- Buff stacking: Add +0.15 to DamageMultiplier per buff
- Gradual drain: Add -0.1 to Hunger per time interval
- Combo scaling: Add +(0.5 * ComboCount) to CritMultiplier
- Percentage tracking: Add +12.5 to QuestCompletionPercent
- Smooth transitions: Add +0.05 to FadeAlpha per frame

Floating-Point Precision:
- Uses double-precision (64-bit) for high accuracy
- Suitable for values ranging from very small (0.0001) to very large (millions)
- Be aware of floating-point rounding for very large accumulated values
- For whole numbers without decimals, prefer Int32 for better performance

@see FGlobalVariableModifier_AddInt32Value for integer addition (whole numbers only)
@see FGameplayProviderNumerical for available value provider types
@see FGlobalVariableType_Numeric for the variable type this modifier operates on
UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_AddTagToContainer:
FGlobalVariableModifier_AddTagToContainer

Modifier that adds a gameplay tag to a tag container global variable.

Behavior:
- If the variable exists: Adds the tag to the existing container (no duplicates)
