UObjectToolTips.FortVehicleModComponent:CollisionLocalSt:
Static meshes that are spawned on the client and server.
These are necessary for welding collision shapes for physics.

These pointers are currently not consistent for replicated variables or RPCs.
There is some complexity about name re-usage with making these net-addressible by unique name,
so for now, refer to query these meshes via their index in the mod config

Any component that is not the root component of an actor, is not considered for component movements.
This means, if we attach a static mesh with collision to a vehicle, it won't affect vehicle handling.
The way to have a mesh affect vehicle handling (ie changing its collision), is by welding it to the vehicle.
This allows us to add additional collision shapes. But note that this is precarious.
 If a shape is added and not welded, intra-collisions can push the vehicle off into the sky as it repeatedly collides with components on itself.

 DO NOT EXPOSE TO BLUEPRINT DIRECTLY. To avoid adding complexity for designer and refactoring, if exposing to blueprint create a query UFUNCTION instead.

UObjectToolTips.MashDifficultyModifierData:
Struct containing data used with DifficultyModifierGE to modify AI attributes (health/damage) based on difficulty level.
When the GE is applied to AI on spawn, magnitude of the modifiers are set with SetSetByCallerMagnitude using the
SetByCallerTag and the calculated magnitude based on the multipliers. The multipliers are looked up based on the
current difficulty level and player count.
Eg, the DifficultyModifierGE could have a damage modifier setup using SetByCaller and tag SetByCaller.Damage. DifficultyModifierData array
would contain an entry of this struct with the same SetByCallerTag and look up table rows for damage multipliers based on the difficulty level and the player count.

Sustained-orbit target speed (cm/s) for projectiles. If > 0, the projectile is driven to spin around the spline at

UObjectToolTips.FortGameplayCueNotify_Loop:
THIS REPLACES FortGameplayCueNotify_Looping
   This is the standard Fort GameplayCue Notify for all looping, duration based cues.
   Anything that has a duration: a distinct start and stop which is defined by the game and not the gameplay cue's assets should use this class.

   Additional features can be built into this class. Anything that is standard and easily defined completey in data is a good candidate. Any new
   thing added should fit into the Application/Looping/Recurring/Removal categories. (E.g., do NOT make new categories or put things outside the
   existing stucture of this class).

   Naming within this class diverges a bit from the rest of the gameplay cue system. For example WhileActive is referred to as Looping within the class.
   These names were chosen as they make the most sense to the FX creators on the development team. Any designer facing features should use these names.

UObjectToolTips.MockFortControllerComponent_EmoteValidat:
Test-only subclass of UFortControllerComponent_EmoteValidation that overrides the
ownership-verification seam to deliver synthetic results. Use this in unit tests where the
validator's behavior must be exercised without a real UFortCosmeticInventoryCache or the
cosmetic inventory subsystem.

Configure the synthetic outcome via SetValidationOutcome before invoking the kickoff. The
override copies the configured outcome and fires it through the supplied OnComplete callback
synchronously.

Test-specific members and the override are wrapped in WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS so the
shipping binary contains only the empty UCLASS shell required for UHT registration; the
class falls through to the base TryStartAsyncOwnershipQuery behavior in non-test builds.

Hidden so the class does not appear in editor pickers / spawn lists; this is a unit-test-only type.

UObjectToolTips.FortQuestCategoryDescriptor:ParentCatego:
The CategoryId of the category this one is listed under -- the authored Parent link, not a
placement guarantee (a record naming an unmaterialized parent routes to the default bucket
client-side until the parent's record appears).
Naming a category here is what makes THAT category a tab. Only ever one level deep: the UI reads a
category and this id, and never follows the parent's own ParentCategoryId to place this record.
Empty by default, which clients read as "no descriptor has arrived yet". Descriptors published by
UFortQuestCategoryRegistrySubsystem::RegisterCategory instead carry
FortQuestPresentation::DefaultQuestTabId (the built-in Quests tab) whenever no parent is honored:
the field is unset, the reflection read fails, or the named parent is not a fort_quest_category
(dropped with a Warning). Only the NAMED PARENT's type is gated here; the publishing category's
own type is the caller convention on RegisterCategory, so an engine quest_category registered
past that convention still carries whatever its inherited Parent yields, fort parent included.
One exception replicates on the wire: a fort category naming ITSELF as Parent carries its own
CategoryId here rather than the sentinel (an engine-typed self-reference is dropped by the
non-fort parent gate first, keeps the sentinel, and never reaches the self-reference Warning);
the UI drops the self-edge when building that tab's sections, and the publish walk ignores it.

UObjectToolTips.FortControllerComponent_AugmentGrantingS:
The Component responsible for augment granting.

//#todo #augments matt.stone revisit this after we have finalized and make sure the comment is true to the actual system.
High level how it works:
        Server
                The server is authoritative on what augments a player can choose.
                        For prototyping, there is a passive GA that randomly chooses augment choices, and gives them to this component for the flow to start.
                        This is pending change, but perhaps it is a good high level way to let design configure augment granting, while leaving most business logic to code.
                It will replicate down to the client the choices it can make, and how many augments it has available.
        Client
                Client gets notified it has available augments and enters a granting flow.
                With augments available, the client can use input to start a selection process, where they pick the augment they want from the available choices.
                        this is currently done via a weapon item; which lets us configure camera modes, etc, while in the augment grant mode.
                Client confirms the choice and lets the server know via server RPC; the server validates and replicates new data to the client.
                Client updates it flow state based on the replicated data from the server (eg new choices, number of pending granting augments)

This AugmentGrantingSystem is intentionally decoupled from the augment component.
Thoughts on the decoupling into separate systems:
        benefits:
                Decoupling keeps the augment system separate from logic granting augments, leading to a more flexible system.
                Decoupling allows us to support different schemes of augment granting without muddying up the actual augment system with code related to obtaining.
                Decoupling allows us to have multiple granting schemes, if needed in the future. It may make sense to have multiple schemes here. But this focuses on choosing from a selection of augments.
                Decoupling means if players obtaining augments via a boss drop in the world, picking up that augment will be separate from this granting management.
                Decoupling means we can have weighted loot tables making augments available, or something else entirely providing the selection of augments available.
                The spytech system was previous investigated for augments, but found that the coupling to round based granting logic made it less flexible (there were other issues as well, such as the type of items spytech was).
                Decoupling means creative can leverage augments without the granting logic; since they will be using their own custom logic.
        negatives:
                it might be slightly more involved to figure out what you need to modify if a change is needed (but I think it shouldn't be too bad, as this keeps classes small).
                we have multiple components where as we could have only 1 without decoupling.
                it could get involved if different components have bad interactions, and need to make components interact with each other (realistically though I think not, since granting augment is done via inventory, these components will hopefully be mutually exclusive).
.

UObjectToolTips.ObjectiveFilter:
The FObjectiveFilter baseclass represents the must-have aspects of any objective filter.  The things common between
all objective filters is that there will Always be an Author that an objective will relate to.
For example, if you shoot someone, 'you' are the instigator of the objective. Inversely if the objective
is Take Damage, and 'you' take damage, you are the instigator for taking damage, even though you are not
the necessarily the damage causer.

Common backup value patterns:

- Merged containers - Combine multiple sources

UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_AddNumericalValue:
The floating-point value to add to the existing variable value

Uses FGameplayProviderNumerical to support both fixed and dynamic values:

Fixed Value Examples:
- ValueToAdd = FixedValue(0.5) - Always add 0.5
- ValueToAdd = FixedValue(-0.1) - Always subtract 0.1
- ValueToAdd = FixedValue(1.0) - Always add 1.0

Dynamic Value Examples:
- ValueToAdd = GlobalVariable(BonusMultiplier) - Add value from another variable
- ValueToAdd = MathOperation(BaseAmount * 1.5) - Calculated bonus
- ValueToAdd = Conditional(HasBonus ? 0.5 : 0.1) - Context-dependent amounts
- ValueToAdd = RandomRange(0.0, 1.0) - Add random floating-point value

Fractional Values:
Supports any double-precision floating-point value:
- Add +0.01 for small increments
- Add -0.5 for half decrements
- Add +3.14159 for precise values

Default is FixedValue(0.0) which adds 0 (no change).

UObjectToolTips.FortSourceWorldAndOverlayWorld:Untracked:
The goal here is to not cook the world when this object is cooked.
To do so I use 2 pointers : one editor only, another one untracked.
The first one used in the editor but is stripped out of the game.
The second one used in game and untracked so it doesn't bring any runtime cook dependency and add redirector dependencies in incremental cook.
Untracked pointers don't get fixed when redirectors are cleaned up that's why I still need the editor only pointer. It's a way to get at the same
time all the editor features of a pointer without adding a cook runtime dependency to the targeted object.

UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableType_Int32:IntValue:
The integer value stored by this global variable

This value is directly read and written by the global variable system through
SetValue() and GetValue() methods.

Default value is 0 to ensure deterministic initialization.

Value Range: -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647 (int32)
UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_AddInt32Value:Val:
The integer value to add to the existing variable value

Uses FGameplayProviderNumerical to support both fixed and dynamic values:

Fixed Value Examples:
- ValueToAdd = FixedValue(1) - Always increment by 1
- ValueToAdd = FixedValue(-10) - Always decrement by 10
- ValueToAdd = FixedValue(100) - Always add 100 points

Dynamic Value Examples:
- ValueToAdd = GlobalVariable(BonusMultiplier) - Add value from another variable
- ValueToAdd = MathOperation(WaveNumber * 5) - Scale with game progression
- ValueToAdd = Conditional(HasBonus ? 50 : 10) - Context-dependent rewards
- ValueToAdd = RandomRange(-5, 5) - Add random variance

Negative Values:
Using negative values allows subtraction without a separate "Subtract" modifier:
- Add -1 to decrement counters
- Add negative damage to health (alternative to separate damage system)
- Add negative values for penalties or costs

Default is FixedValue(0.0) which adds 0 (no change).

UObjectToolTips.FortWeaponRanged:AimPitchMax:
The maximum aim pitch allowed.
     Limits how high a shot can be fired. Could be used for a mortar style weapon and/or and can prevent shots from being fired straight up or even backwards.
     This can ensure that projectiles are fired with a heading that is near the camera's/muzzle's forward heading.
     (Common situations where a projectile's heading is far from expectations: 1) If the weapon is aimed very near straight up/down where a small amount of spread can radically change the projectile heading, or 2) Where ProjectilePitchOffset can cause the projectile to be fired at a pitch more than 90 degrees from 0 which essentially reverses the heading.)
     For projectile weapons: when aim pitch is clamped ProjectilePitchOffset is taken into account before clamping.
     Set >= 180 to disable.
     Data validation will fail is NOT AimPitchMin <= AimPitchMax.

The minimum aim pitch allowed.
     Limits how low a shot can be fired. Could be used for a mortar style weapon and/or can prevent shots from being fired straight down or even backwards.
     This can ensure that projectiles are fired with a heading that is near the camera's/muzzle's forward heading.
     (Common situations where a projectile's heading is far from expectations: 1) If the weapon is aimed very near straight up/down where a small amount of spread can radically change the projectile heading, or 2) Where ProjectilePitchOffset can cause the projectile to be fired at a pitch more than 90 degrees from 0 which essentially reverses the heading.)
     For projectile weapons: when aim pitch is clamped ProjectilePitchOffset is taken into account before clamping.
     Set <= -180 to disable.
     Data validation will fail is NOT AimPitchMin <= AimPitchMax.

UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_SetInt32Value:New:
The new integer value to set the variable to

Uses FGameplayProviderNumerical to support both fixed and dynamic values:

Fixed Value Example (design-time):
- NewValue = FixedValue(100) - Always sets variable to 100

Dynamic Value Examples (runtime):
- NewValue = GlobalVariable(ScoreTag) - Copy value from another variable
- NewValue = MathOperation(CurrentValue * 2) - Double the existing value
- NewValue = RandomRange(1, 10) - Set to random value

For modifying existing values relative to current value:
- Option 1: Use AddInt32Value modifier (simpler for addition/subtraction)
- Option 2: Use provider with math operations: MathOperation(GlobalVariable(MyTag) + 10)

Default is FixedValue(0.0) which sets the variable to 0.

UObjectToolTips.FortEventReaction_UpdateNumericVariable::
The numerical provider used to multiply the update amount

Only used when bUseMultiplier is true. The provider is evaluated at reaction time
and its result is multiplied with the conditional delta.

Formula: FinalAmount = Delta * MultiplierValue (both doubles, full precision)

Common multiplier patterns:
- FixedValue(2.0) - Double the delta
- FixedValue(0.5) - Halve the delta
- FixedValue(1.25) - Apply 125% of delta (25% bonus)
- GlobalVariable(EventMultiplier) - Scale by event bonus
- MathOperation(1.0 + BonusPercent) - Additive bonus calculation

Note: All calculations preserve double precision - no truncation.
Example: Delta=0.125 * Multiplier=1.5 = 0.1875 (exact result)
UObjectToolTips.FortEventReaction_UpdateInt32Variable:Nu:
The numerical provider used to multiply the update amount

Only used when bUseMultiplier is true. The provider is evaluated at reaction time
and its result is multiplied with the conditional delta.

Formula: FinalAmount = static_cast<int32>(Delta * MultiplierValue)

Common multiplier patterns:
- FixedValue(2.0) - Double the delta
- FixedValue(0.5) - Halve the delta
- GlobalVariable(DifficultyMultiplier) - Scale by difficulty
- Conditional provider - Different multipliers based on conditions
- MathOperation(TeamSize) with reciprocal - Divide among team

Note: Both delta and multiplier result are converted to int32, truncating fractions.
Example: Delta=10.7 * Multiplier=1.5 = 16.05 → 16 (int32)

UObjectToolTips.GlobalVariableModifier_Int32MathOperatio:
The operand value for the mathematical operation

Uses FGameplayProviderNumerical to support both fixed and dynamic operands:

Fixed Value Examples:
- OperandValue = FixedValue(2) - Double (multiply) or halve (divide)
- OperandValue = FixedValue(10) - Scale by 10 (multiply) or wrap 0-9 (modulo)
- OperandValue = FixedValue(4) - Quarter the value (divide by 4)

Dynamic Value Examples:
- OperandValue = GlobalVariable(DifficultyMultiplier) - Scale by difficulty
- OperandValue = MathOperation(PlayerCount) - Divide by player count
- OperandValue = Conditional(IsHardMode ? 3 : 2) - Context-dependent scaling

Safety Notes:
- For Divide/Modulo: Zero operand is handled safely (preserves value, logs warning)
- For Multiply: Large values can overflow (standard C++ integer wrapping)

Default is FixedValue(1.0) which multiplies by 1 (no change), divides by 1 (no change),
or modulo by 1 (always results in 0).

UObjectToolTips.ApplyWrapVariantDef:MetaTags:
The set of meta tags this variant specifies.
Used in LTMs which want to apply custom part overrides (Wick/Bounty)

MetaTags are applied with the main cosmetic definition tags as a base.
Any currently active MetaTags can either add additional tags or remove tags.
All active variants can remove/add tags (processed in a loop)

Use Cases:
             Variant of Peely with a painted-on suit.
                     (Remove ExtremelyUnique, add Assassin)
                     Results in Bounty leaving the skin alone (ignore that we do that anyway).

             Variant of Reaper, but he's wearing golf attire (or something).
                     (Remove Assassin)
                     Results in Bounty forcing that variant into a suit (as per any other outfit).
                     Reaper's primary variant would keep his suit.

@see MetaTags on the main cosmetic item definition (scroll up).

UObjectToolTips.FortEventReaction_ModifyTagContainer:Tag:
The tags to add, remove, or set

Interpretation depends on Operation:
- **Add**: These tags are added to the existing container
- **Remove**: These tags are removed from the container if present
- **Set**: The container is replaced with exactly these tags
- **Clear**: This field is ignored (container is emptied regardless)

Can contain multiple tags for batch operations:
- Add {"Buff.Strength", "Buff.Speed"} grants both buffs at once
- Remove {"Debuff.Slowed", "Debuff.Weakened"} clears multiple debuffs
- Set {"Permission.View", "Permission.Edit"} establishes exact permissions

Examples:
- Grant damage buff: Add operation with tags {"Buff.Damage.Tier1"}
- Remove poison: Remove operation with tags {"Status.Poison"}
- Set admin perms: Set operation with tags {"Perm.Admin", "Perm.Edit", "Perm.Delete"}

UObjectToolTips.PlayspaceComponent_DispatchExternallyRea:
This PlayspaceComponent is part of the 'InferPlayspaceReachability' system, and exists to signal to external code that the Playspace it exists within is now "Externally Discoverable".

Add this component to your Playspace when you want to use WaitForDiscoverablePlayspaceWithFilterAction / GameStateComponent_ListenForExternallyReachablePlayspaces.

A Playspace is "Externally Discoverable" on the server when it has been inserted into the Playspace Tree (OnPlayspaceCreatedAndReady).
A Playspace is "Externally Discoverable" on the clients when the Parent Playspace (on the client) has had its ChildPlayspace array replicated to include the new Child Playspace (or if it is known to be the RootPlayspace of the Playspace Manager).

In other words, if you start from RootPlayspace->GetChildPlayspaces()... and were to recursively append all GetChildPlayspaces arrays into a single array, then a Playspace is "Externally Discoverable" if it exists in that array (or is the root).

This component type handles all of this for you, on either Servers or Clients, and provides a statically available delegate for when any Playspace (which has this component) first becomes Externally Discoverable.

@See UWaitForDiscoverablePlayspaceWithFilterAction
@See UGameStateComponent_ListenForExternallyReachablePlayspaces

UObjectToolTips.SkyfireTODOverrideVolume:
This class represents a 'null' gameplay volume which will house a FortVolumeTimeOfDayComponent. The TOD component
will be enabled/disabled by manually broadcasting player entered/exited events from SkyfireControllerComponent and
will not be enabled/disabled by any actor/player actually entering or exiting the volume. Though this class implements
IFortSpatialGameplayInterface, it does not provide useful implementations of the functions in that interface as it
is meant to act as a volume with infinitely small bounds (i.e. a 'null' volume).

The reason this class is necessary is that in order for FortVolumeTimeOfDayComponents to work properly, they must be
attached to a GameplayVolume actor that implements IFortSpatialGameplayInterface. Skyfire cannot use the typical FortVolume
that is used by other TOD components because the TOD will automatically enable/disable based on if the player is inside
the volume.

UObjectToolTips.UnicornDriver:
This class will drive the unicorn process - being the central point of storage for information on players, as well as their highlights
Each player is given a log, which will record their movements, build events, eliminations/deaths etc
When an elimination occurs, the Driver will log it down, and then use a series of Evaluators to determine how interesting the elimination is
Each evaluator will judge the elimination based off the player's Log, and the elimination information available
Each evaluator will judge the elimination and give it a score based off what they are interested in, and when such a highlight clip should start and stop
Evaluators combine their assessment of an EvaluatedElimination, and a highlight clip is created from it
Highlight clips are saved to a players log. Any highlight clips that are close together get merged together
At the end of the game, the server extracts an significant highlights according to what BaseHighlightExtractors are enabled
Highlight extractors make new highlight clips, or look at existing ones and say "I don't care about the score, this is an important clip!"
The server gathers all highlight clips from all players, and sorts them based off score (what the evaluators say about an interesting kill) and significance (what the Extractors say)
The top N game highlights are made into replay camera shots, and saved to the replay file

UObjectToolTips.FortPhysicsPickup:
This is a pickup class that uses simulated physics for movement, instead of the projectile movement component.
In order to use this (assuming using from a plugin), the following is needed...

1. Create a custom BP pickup class.
2. Add an "Override Pickup Class" Game Feature Action to force the game to use a different pick up class.
3. Create a FortPhysicsObjectPreset asset in your plugin to be used by your physics pickup.
4. Create a UFortPhysicsObjectPreset asset in your plugin to be used by your physics pickup.
5. Added a "Physics Object Setup Data" Game Feature Action to your plugin and configure to point at the two previous assets you created.
6. Update your pickup BP class "Physics Object Tag" properties to point at the tags you referenced in the previous step.

UObjectToolTips.FortVersionedSparseClassData:
This struct is to be used in any sparse class data structs that want to support
      versioning for moving data into the sparse class data more than once.  In order
      to use this, subclasses will need to define the following static const inline...

      static const inline FFortSparseClassDataVersionInfo VersionInfo{TEXT("MyStructName"), 1};

      As well, you will need to add the function in the classes that use the versioned sparse class data...

      FORTNITEGAME_API virtual void MoveDataToSparseClassDataStructCustom(bool bIsSaving = false) const;

      This function will need to be called in MoveDataToSparseClassDataStruct, passing in false. And also
      called in PreSave, passing in true.

      To ensure versioned data migrates between related struct types, Conform must be called by the class implementation of:

      virtual bool ConformSparseClassDataStruct(UScriptStruct* const SourceSparseClassDataStruct, void* SourceSparseClassData) const override;

      NOTE:   The copy constructors are explicitly NOT copying any data. This ensures data from this struct is NEVER copied
                      from a class archetype instance. This data NEEDS to be unique per UClass instance. If this is not true,
                      this struct will not properly control when sparse class data does or does NOT copy data from deprecated class properties.
                      The only time version data should be copied is during ConformSparseClassDataStruct, when it calls Conform.

      Each time a child class adds more data, it will need to increase the version number in the VersionInfo.
      For an example of how to use this, please look at ABuildingActor and FBuildingActorClassData, along with
      all of it's subclasses.  For further questions, please reach out to @andrew.thayer.

UObjectToolTips.FortEvenlySizedSegment:
This structure contains a list of evenly sized segments, meaning their end points are roughly "evenly spaced" along the trail constituted by the PathToDestination points.
It also contains the necessary info for calculating and setting up the associated spline mesh and its associated collision.
This is not replicated.  It is written to be initialized and kept only on the client as the client received points in PathToDestination from the server.
While the points that make up the spline are meant to be static, there is some handling of interpolation of the end point, growth alphas, etc.

UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindDirect: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals.  This angle is the value in degrees to be added on either side of the area that should be considered a cardinal direction when trying to find clouds in those directions.  We need additional angle because the clouds are on a grid formed over where the rifts form, and those are already random and may be near the edge of the relevant cone.
UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindActive: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals. UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindInacti: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals. UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindFallof: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals.  This radius is the distance around the outer perimeter of the storm wind over which the wind falls off from full wind to nothing.
UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindGoalRa: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals.  This radius is the extra buffer around the primary encounter goal actors that needs to be guaranteed to be covered in wind.
UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindCloudR: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals.  This radius is the extra buffer around the storm clouds that needs to be guaranteed to be covered in wind.
UObjectToolTips.FortThreatVisualsManager:StormWindDesire: ThreatVisuals handles creating 'storm winds' for encounters; these winds cover the area from the far side of the threat clouds to the opposite side of the encounter goals.  This time is time in seconds over which the wind will change whenever a change occurs (such as when clouds form, when they activate or deactivate, and when they die.  NOTE: This time is just a suggested time.  If the wind covers too large of an area, it may take more time to change in order to keep performance reasonable.

UObjectToolTips.EPoseBuilderAlphaBlendType:
Time-blending shape used by `FPoseBuilderAlphaInterpConfig`. Lets the rigger pick between
the engine's standard exponential `FInterpTo` and a linear ramp matching `BlendListByBool`.

Exponential (default): interped += (target - interped) * Speed * DT each tick. Smooth, no
fixed completion time, lower overshoot risk. Default used by all existing PoseBuilder usage.

Linear: interped advances toward target by `Speed * DT` per tick (clamped). Reproduces the
UE BlendListByBool behavior where Speed = 1/BlendDuration. Use when matching a source that
has a known blend duration (e.g. AnimBP `AlphaBoolBlend(BlendInTime=0.2,BlendOutTime=0.2)`
→ Speed = 5).

state that used to live as scattered UPROPERTY(Transient) members on the asset itself, plus
the per-asset UI state that used to live as static members on FPoseBuilderAssetDetails.

Lives by value on the asset (no separate UObject, no allocation, no null check). Never
serialized — the entire struct resets on editor restart, matching the prior Transient semantics.

Why a struct, not a class:
  - Value semantics → access is always `Asset->EditorState.X`, never null.
  - One instance per asset → multi-window editing of different assets is correctly isolated
    (vs. the old static fields which leaked between asset details panels).
  - Two panels for the same asset still share the same state (correct: same data).
  - In cooked builds the few hundred bytes are unused but harmless; this avoids scattering
    #if WITH_EDITORONLY_DATA / #if WITH_EDITOR around every read site.

UObjectToolTips.EPoseBuilderPoseState:
Tri-state enable for a pose. Cycled via right-click on the gear button.
- Active:         normal evaluation, output written, slider/override respected.
- OutputDisabled: driver bones / curves / operations are NOT calculated, and the
                  pose's contribution is NOT written to driven bones — but the user's
                  PoseBlendWeights / ActivatedPoseBlendSlots / FullActivationHistory
                  entries are preserved so re-enabling restores the prior slider state.
- Inactive:       same skip behavior as OutputDisabled, plus the pose's slider/override
                  state is reset to zero on entry. The pose row's expanded details are
                  fully hidden in this state.
UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderKeyPose:PoseState:
Tri-state pose enable. Replaces the old bDisabled bool with three distinct levels:
Active = full evaluation + output; OutputDisabled = skip eval and output, preserve
the user's slider/override values; Inactive = skip everything and reset the slider/
override to zero. The gear button cycles through these via right-click.

UObjectToolTips.FortAttachableProjectileComponent:
UFortAttachableProjectileComponent:
Component to support projectiles that attach to their target. The attachment must be initiated by the projectile's
authority calling AuthorityAttachToActor typically in blueprint in response to the OnTouched event. The the attachment
params are replicated to other nodes. The exact attachment location is determined separately on each client based on
the hit location and the client's animation state. The attachment location on the server will be the target's origin.
This component can be used with AFortProjectileBase (which does uses the server side capsule collision volume for
initial hit detection), or the newer AFortProjectileAthena (which offers more precise hit detection using the owning
player's mesh collision volume). Any other actor class with a ProjectileMovementComponent can utilize this component
for basic projectile attachment functionality.
The logic for this component is mostly ported from AFortAttachableProjectileDeprecated, which is now deprecated in
favor of this component. The motivation for pulling the logic into a component was to allow it to be shared amongst
different projectile actor types.
Note that if we notice attachment latency especially with client side predicted or athena projectiles, we can refine
this algorithm. All attachment is initiated server side at the moment.

UObjectToolTips.ETasksOverFramesSchedulePriorityCategory:
UTasksOverFramesScheduleManager.cpp: A manager to split work over multiple
frames to reduce frame hitches.  Any function can be added to this queue
and it will be called back based when frame time is available, likely within
a few frames.

NOTE: All functions queued via this manager will appear as part of CharacterCustomization in Perf reports
for the time being. Contact #fn-pi-cosmetics-tech-ext if that is undesired for your use case.

The manager uses a priority queue to decide on what to work on next.
Priority is determined by a Category (feel free to add more) and a
SubPriority     within that Priority.  The SubPriority can be different
depending on the category.  For some it might be based on how visible
something is to the camera for example, for others some other heuristic might
be used.

There are various ways to configure TasksOverFramesScheduleManager with CVars.
See CVars in the CPP.

Note the complexity of this class is the result of trying to make sure we cover future use
such as cases:
 - Reentrant functions where a callback tries to do work in a callback
 - Lifetime of objects who own the function pointer
 - Making sure we don't accidentally skip a callback call by replacing it
 - Doing work immediately if we are still within the budget so we can see things a frame
 - earlier
 - Preventing users from accidentally making a copy of the handle

=============================================================================// List of priorities types the higher in the list the higher the priority

UObjectToolTips.LootInjectionOptionRow:UpgradesAtTokenCo:
Upgrade track for this loot option.
When a player hits the key token count, they will gain a "level" in the specified upgrade.
This is cumulative, so the player has all the upgrades on the track that they have unlocked previously at lower token counts.
Example:
2, SpawnChance
4, SpawnChance
8, Rarity
At token count 1, the player will have unlocked this loot option using the base LTG and base spawn chance.
At 2 and 3, they will have level 1 upgraded spawn chance, using SpawnChanceUpgrades[0] instead of the base spawn chance.
At 4 - 7, they will have level 2 upgraded spawn chance (SpawnChanceUpgrades[1])
At 8, they will have level 2 upgraded spawn chance (SpawnChanceUpgrades[1]) AND level 1 rarity upgrade (RarityUpgrades[0])

UObjectToolTips.OratorDialogCorrectionSettings:Punctuati:
Used to clean up concatenated punctuation (i.e. "...,!?.!,..." => "?") when bCorrectPunctuation is enabled.
The order of the characters in the string matter to define priority.

All adjacent punctuation characters will be removed to keep a single punctuation character
- Exception: three-periods-ellipsis (will account for a single punctuation char)
In case of different adjacent characters (i.e. "?!!"), only the last character found in @PunctuationCleanupString is kept.
- Example (with PunctuationCleanupString = ",.(U+2026 ellipsis)!?"): "Well,, wait..... Huh...?!" => "Well, wait... Huh?"

Used to convert changes in upward speed to changes in suspension tension. SuspensionTensionToSpeedScalar * 1uu/seconds == 1 tension unit.
     Set to 0.0 to disable suspension.
     When enabled the suspension system will add tension when the projectile is deflected and loses/gains upward velocity.
     When the suspension system has tension, tension will be removed every frame in TickComponent() and velocity will be added in the opposite direction. This allows the system to mitigate bounces and small curbs acting like ramps.

UObjectToolTips.XpDetails:
Used to track specific details about xp gained from reactions with a given SourceId. Multiple grants that have the same SourceId will be combined into a single FXpDetails object.

Example quest payload (single completion awarded 1k base + 25% bonus from Boosters)
               Source ID: Quest:sparksquest_prestige_pc_ag_01b
               Source Type: Quest
               Base Xp Gained: 1000
               Rested XP Consumed: 0
               Boosters XP: 250
               Grant Count: 1
               BoostedBonusXpDetails:
                       [0] ItemId=instance-uuid-1, TemplateId=XpBooster:DefaultBooster, BoostedBonusXp=250
Example Accolade Payload (a single accolade that was triggered twice, each trigger awarding 1k base + 1k rested + 25% bonus from Boosters)
               Source ID: 77450984B2D5337AB6EA70FED8A685CE:3:255:0
               Source Type: Accolade
               Base Xp Gained: 2000
               Rested XP Consumed: 2000
               Boosters XP: 500
               Grant Count: 2
               BoostedBonusXpDetails:
                       [0] ItemId=instance-uuid-1, TemplateId=XpBooster:DefaultBooster, BoostedBonusXp=400
                       [1] ItemId=instance-uuid-2, TemplateId=XpBooster:WeekendBooster, BoostedBonusXp=100
                       // Per-entry BoostedBonusXp accumulates across the two merged grants via sum-into-kept on ItemId; sum equals BoostedBonusXp (audit-trail invariant).

UObjectToolTips.FortVisibilityManagerComponent:
VisibilityManager

      This manager handles looping through all visibility infos and checking if each
      observer can see that info and if so marks the info and syncs it to all clients.

      The visibility manager has a 1 to 1 relationship to the visibility components. A
      component will automatically register its owner actor with the manager and if the
      component is marked for observing then that actor will be registered as an observer
      too. This is normally reserved for Players, and if we have almost everything observers
      we should change this tech a bit...

      ObserverArray - The list of observers that all info's check against.
      VisibilityInfoArray - The array of infos that are sync'ed to the clients indicating an
                                                Actors visibility.

We will compare the TPM of a dynamic xp source, and find the highest possible TPMFloor that's lower. The weight of the source will be multiplied

UObjectToolTips.FortProjectileMoveComp_Slider:bSuspensio:
When set to true allows downward tension to be added on deflection and eased every tick. Downward tension is built up when the projectile gains downward velocity after a deflection, downward tension will add upward velocity to the projectile over time; might be useful to minimize jumping curbs in uncommon gravity situations.
     Turning this on can cause the projectile to build up suspension while sliding on the ground and cause it to jump, especially if a lot of gravity gets dumped into the velocity during a fire rate spike.
     If disabled tension will not update nor build in the downward direction. Tension will ease every frame as long as bSuspensionEnabled_Up or bSuspensionEnabled_Down is enabled.

When set to true allows upward tension to be added on deflection and eased every tick. Upward tension is built up when the projectile gains upward velocity after a deflection, upward tension will add downward velocity to the projectile over time; this is a good way to minimize jumping curbs.
     If disabled tension will not update nor build in the upward direction. Tension will ease every frame as long as bSuspensionEnabled_Up or bSuspensionEnabled_Down is enabled.

UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderAimMathDrivenConfig:bMaintain:
When true (default), preserves the bone's REST orientation as the "zero" aim state —
the runtime computes a one-tick OffsetRotation from initial transforms + initial
target resolution, then post-multiplies it into the live aim result. Net effect:
at rest (targets at rest, parent at rest), the aim is a no-op regardless of the
authored Axis, Target, TargetSpace, or Kind. Changes to those parameters at rest
do NOT pop the bone — the offset rebakes the new authored intent against rest state.

if the rigger wants the aim to drive the bone all the way from its rest orientation
to the authored target direction at full weight (no offset preservation).

UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderKeyPose:bStatic:
When true, the pose is treated as an always-on baseline correction. Skips all driver
evaluation — DriverBones / DriverCurveEntries / Operations / PoseWeightVariable are
IGNORED and the pose applies at full strength every tick. Mirrors the source-rig pattern
of ModifyTransforms_PerItem / SetTransform / ParentConstraint with a literal Weight=1.0
and no Weight pin wire — those nodes fire unconditionally at runtime.

Evaluation ORDER: static poses are applied BEFORE the regular (driver-evaluated) pass on
every tick. Any non-static pose that drives the same bone layers ON TOP of the static
result, not the other way around — the static value is the baseline floor that driver
poses blend from. See FRigUnit_PoseBuilder_Execute.
UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderDriverCurveEntry:bInterpResul:
When true, the post-remap output value is exponentially interpolated each tick toward
the live curve value at `InterpResultSpeed`. Mirrors `AlphaScaleBiasClamp::bInterpResult`
on AnimGraph nodes — useful when the source value is noisy and you want the pose's
output to track it smoothly. Default false.
UObjectToolTips.PoseBuilderOperation:bDebugEnabled:
When true, the runtime draws this operation's manifold (Distance arrow / AxisProjection
ray / etc) while the pose's normal-mode manifold visibility rules allow it.

Defaults to false so newly-deserialized ops (including public ops, Reference ops,
and ops loaded from older saves) start with the manifold hidden. The add-op paths in
PoseBuilderAssetDetails_DriverOps.cpp explicitly set this true for the user-facing
private op types (Distance, AxisProjection); Reference ops keep false; public-op
promotion keeps false (the runtime auto-shows public op manifolds when a manually-
activated consumer pose references them, so the eye toggle defaults off for less
viewport clutter).

We expect to have a valid index for that property to be added to this map via AddGeneratePathPropertyNestedIndexData
Example lets say you are looking for property bCount for Objective 2 the path would be Objectives[2]->bCount
Auto generation how ever doesn't know it has to look for Index = 2. So in this case we need to specify that for Property Objectives we are looking for Index 2

If false: The delta is applied directly without modification

Use cases for multipliers:
- Difficulty scaling: Multiply by difficulty factor
- Bonus periods: Apply 2x or 3x multipliers
- Team splits: Divide among team members
- Percentage modifiers: Apply fractional adjustments

UObjectToolTips.FortEventReaction_UpdateNumericVariable::
Whether to multiply the update amount by a numerical provider value

If true: The delta is multiplied by the evaluated NumericalMultiplier before applying
If false: The delta is applied directly without modification

Use cases for multipliers:
- Efficiency scaling: Multiply by efficiency factor (0.8 = 20% reduction)
- Bonus periods: Apply 1.5x or 2.0x multipliers
- Fractional adjustments: Apply percentage modifiers
- Dynamic scaling: Scale based on game state variables

Default is false (no multiplier).

UObjectToolTips.FortAthenaMutator_SE_HoldWinConditionFor:
While active, fires OnRiftAnomalySuppressionChanged so the owning event Blueprint can pause rift-anomaly spawning and clear active
anomalies. Rift anomalies have no C++ disable API in this codebase (the disable path is Blueprint only), so the Blueprint relay is
required to actually take effect. On by default.

While active, hides the quest/challenge, XP and accolade HUD feeds via the HUD hide-tag system (client side) - this is how XP/quest
"contents" are suppressed for the event (the UI is hidden; backend progression is intentionally not touched). Urgent-quest and FTUE
prompt widgets use Blueprint-authored HUD tags that are not registered natively, so pin those per event in ExtraHideUITags. In-match
FTUE spawning itself is governed by the ContextTutorial system (bEnableContextTutorial), not by this mutator. On by default.

While active, suppresses in-match event notifications/announcements (AFortPlayerController::SuppressEventNotifications, server side).
Reverted on deactivate/teardown. On by default.

UObjectToolTips.FortCharacterDynamicsComponentInterface:
class UFortCharacterDynamicsComponentInterface

Provides an abstract interface for the UFortCharacterDynamicsComponent Actor Component that excludes any
references to structures defined in FortniteGame (specifically AnimInstances etc). This class exists purely
to solve dependency problems and allow features of the Character Dynamics Control plugin to be accessed by
FortniteGame code and assets.

This class uses a pure non-virtual interface to work around the limitations of UFunction declarations
(they can't be virtual).
